entries.title: Paint on my nose
entries.body: I cried when mommy left at preschool. Miss Joy holded my hand. And then we painted and I painted a big sun with lellow and orange. And I got paint on my nose and Ava laughed and I laughed too.
entries.highlight: Cried at preschool drop-off, then painted a sun with Miss Joy's help and laughed with her friend Ava.

entries.title: Gummy bears in the car
entries.body: After preschool mommy gave me gummy bears in the car. I ate a red one and a green one and a red one again. I made one dance like a real bear. And then goldfish crackers. My tummy was happy.
entries.highlight: Had a gummy bear snack after preschool and pretended they were real dancing bears.

entries.title: I was the grandma
entries.body: I played grandmas at grandma's house. I was the grandma and grandma was the little girl. I wore her glasses and everything was blurry. I made pretend tea and we ate the leftover pie from Thanksgiving. Real pie.
entries.highlight: Played her favorite pretend game, grandmas, wearing Grandma's glasses and serving pretend tea with leftover pie.

entries.title: First sled day
entries.body: It snowed! Brett took me sledding on the little hill. We went so fast and I falled off in the snow and my face got cold. It's Sunday. Sunday is my favorite day because that's kind of my name.
entries.highlight: Went sledding with big brother Brett on the first snow and explained that Sunday is her favorite day.

entries.title: Milk came out my nose
entries.body: At dinner Brett made a frog face with his cheeks. I laughed so hard milk came out my nose. Mommy said Brett. Brett said sorry Sunny Bunny. He calls me Sunny Bunny. He is my big brother and he is ten.
entries.highlight: Laughed so hard at Brett's frog face at dinner that milk came out her nose; Brett calls her Sunny Bunny.

entries.title: Circle time song
entries.body: At circle time we sang the snowflake song. I sat next to Ava on the blue square. Ben was wiggly and Miss Joy said criss cross applesauce. I didn't cry today. Only a little in the car.
entries.highlight: Sang a snowflake song at preschool circle time next to Ava and cried only a little before drop-off.

entries.title: Grandma's tiny tree
entries.body: I helped grandma put the ornaments on her tiny tree. I put all of them on the bottom because I am small. Grandma said it was perfect. Her back hurts so she sat in the rocking chair and pointed.
entries.highlight: Helped Grandma decorate her small tree, placing every ornament on the low branches.

entries.title: Strawberry ice cream in the cold
entries.body: We got ice cream even though it is cold outside. I got strawberry ice cream with rainbow sprinkles. Pink is the best flavor. Daddy said what flavor is pink and I said pink flavor. It dripped on my mitten.
entries.highlight: Ate her favorite strawberry ice cream with rainbow sprinkles with Dad on a cold winter day.

entries.title: Tag in the basement
entries.body: It was too cold outside so me and Brett played tag in the basement. Brett is fast but he runs slow for me. I tagged him on the couch. And then he tagged me and I hided under the stairs.
entries.highlight: Played tag with Brett in the basement, where he slowed down so she could catch him.

entries.title: A snowman with a pink hat
entries.body: At preschool we painted snowmen. My snowman has a pink hat and three buttons. Mia's snowman had a carrot nose. Miss Joy hanged them on the wall. I'm gonna show mommy tomorrow at pickup.
entries.highlight: Painted a snowman with a pink hat at preschool, and Miss Joy displayed it on the wall.

entries.title: Snowman named Mister Cold
entries.body: More snow! Brett and me made a snowman in the front yard. I named him Mister Cold. I gave him my old mittens for hands. Brett put a stick for a mouth. Then we had hot cocoa with tiny marshmallows.
entries.highlight: Built a snowman named Mister Cold with Brett and warmed up with hot cocoa.

entries.title: Brett read the reindeer book
entries.body: This morning Brett read me the reindeer book in my bed. He did the voices. The reindeer voice was so funny and low. I pointed at the pictures. I know the R. R is for reindeer.
entries.highlight: Brett read her a reindeer book on Christmas Eve morning, doing voices while she pointed out the letter R.

entries.title: Cookies for Santa
entries.body: Tonight me and mommy put cookies on a plate for Santa. And carrots for the reindeers. Then we cuddled on the couch with the tree lights on. Mommy smells like cookies. I am too excited to sleep.
entries.favorite: Cuddling with the tree lights on
entries.highlight: Set out cookies and carrots for Santa with Mom and cuddled by the tree lights on Christmas Eve.

entries.title: Christmas!
entries.body: Christmas! It snowed in the night. I got a unicorn stuffie and her name is Sparkle like my pretend horse. Brett took me sledding and snowboarding. I sat on the snowboard and he pulled me. I didn't fall. Well one time.
entries.highlight: Got a unicorn stuffie named Sparkle for Christmas, then went sledding and snowboarding with Brett in fresh snow.

entries.title: My new unicorn coloring book
entries.body: I colored in my new unicorn coloring book from Christmas. I made the unicorn purple and the rainbow every color. I went outside the lines a little. Sparkle the stuffie watched me color.
entries.highlight: Spent a cozy day coloring in her new unicorn coloring book with her stuffie Sparkle beside her.

entries.title: Sprinkle cookies
entries.body: Me and mommy made sugar cookies. I did the sprinkles. I did a lot of sprinkles. Mommy said that's a sprinkle mountain. I licked the spoon. The star cookie broke so I ate it.
entries.highlight: Baked sugar cookies with Mom and was in charge of very generous sprinkles.

entries.title: Tag around the kitchen
entries.body: Me and Brett played tag around the kitchen island. Round and round and round. I got dizzy and falled down and laughed. Mommy said no running in the kitchen. So we walked fast.
entries.highlight: Played tag with Brett around the kitchen island until she got dizzy, then switched to fast walking.

entries.title: Purple sparkle nails
entries.body: Mommy painted my nails purple sparkle. I had to sit still and blow on them. I blowed so hard. Then I got one smudge on my pinky. Mommy fixed it. Now my hands are fancy.
entries.highlight: Mom painted her nails purple with sparkles, and she worked hard to sit still while they dried.

entries.title: New Year pajama day
entries.body: Yesternight was New Year and I tried to stay up but I falled asleep on the couch. Today was a pajama day. I stayed in my unicorn pajamas all day long and watched a movie and ate toast.
entries.highlight: Fell asleep before midnight on New Year's Eve and spent New Year's Day in her pajamas.

entries.title: Brett wore my tiara
entries.body: Brett wore my tiara and said he is the princess of the house. I said no you're not, I am. He did a twirl and his socks slipped. I laughed and laughed. Brett is so silly.
entries.highlight: Brett wore her tiara and twirled around pretending to be a princess, which made her laugh.

entries.title: Library book about a cat
entries.body: Mommy and me went to the library after preschool. I picked a book with a orange cat. The cat is called Pickle. I want a thousand cats. Mommy said one book at a time. I got two books.
entries.highlight: Picked out a picture book about an orange cat at the library with Mom and repeated her wish for a thousand cats.

entries.title: Grandma's purple shawl
entries.body: I played grandmas again. I wore grandma's purple shawl and walked slow and said oh my back. Grandma laughed so much. She said is that what I sound like. I said yes grandma.
entries.highlight: Played grandmas wearing Grandma's shawl and copied her walk, which made Grandma laugh.

entries.title: Snow angel in the yard
entries.body: I made a snow angel in the backyard. I moved my arms and legs and it was a angel. Then I stood up and stepped on her wing. Oops. I made another one. Two angels.
entries.highlight: Made snow angels in the backyard and fixed the first one by making a second.

entries.title: Sick day with mommy
entries.body: I had a cough so I didn't go to preschool. Mommy let me lay on her lap and she rubbed my back. We watched the cat show. I had soup with the little stars in it. Being sick is not fun but cuddles are.
entries.highlight: Stayed home sick from preschool and spent the day cuddling with Mom and eating star soup.

entries.title: Slow motion tag
entries.body: Tonight Brett said I can't run because I'm sick so we played slow motion tag. We moved super super slow like turtles. Brett made a slow motion face. It was the best tag ever.
entries.highlight: Brett invented slow motion tag so she could play while she was home sick.

entries.title: I got grandma a blanket
entries.body: Grandma came to watch me because I'm still coughing. She was cold so I got her my fuzzy blanket. It's a little small for a grandma. She put it on her knees. She said thank you sweet pea.
entries.highlight: Brought Grandma her own fuzzy blanket when Grandma felt cold during a babysitting day.

entries.title: Lunchbox surprise
entries.body: Mommy put gummy bears in my lunchbox for a surprise! I shared one with Zoe. Zoe likes the orange ones and I like the red ones. So we traded. That is a good trade.
entries.highlight: Found gummy bears in her lunchbox and traded colors with her friend Zoe.

entries.title: Resting with Sparkle
entries.body: Tonight I'm resting in my bed with Sparkle. Sparkle is tired because she galloped all day. I put her under my blanket. I'm a little bit tired too. Night night.
entries.highlight: Wound down at bedtime by tucking in her unicorn Sparkle.

entries.title: Sunday ice cream
entries.body: It is Sunday so we got ice cream. Strawberry with rainbow sprinkles. Brett got chocolate with nuts. Yuck. I gave Brett one lick of mine. He said pink tastes like bubble gum. No it tastes like Sunday. Sunday is kind of my name.
entries.highlight: Shared a lick of her strawberry ice cream with Brett on a Sunday outing.

entries.title: Snow day fort
entries.body: No preschool because of snow. Me and Brett made a blanket fort with all the couch pillows. It's called Fort Sunny. Only people with a password can come in. The password is gummy bear.
entries.highlight: Built Fort Sunny out of blankets and couch pillows with Brett on a snow day.

entries.title: Every nail a different color
entries.body: Mommy painted my nails every color. Pink and purple and blue and lellow and green. Like a rainbow on my hands. I showed Miss Joy at preschool and she said wow.
entries.highlight: Mom painted each of her nails a different color and she proudly showed her teacher.

entries.title: Quiet day
entries.body: Today was a quiet day. I didn't want to do anything. I just layed on the floor and looked at the ceiling and the fan going round. Then I had apple slices. Quiet days are nice.
entries.highlight: Had a quiet, slow day at home lying on the floor and snacking on apple slices.

entries.title: Big squeeze hug
entries.body: Mommy picked me up from preschool and gave me a big squeeze hug. I missed her all day. I told her I didn't cry at all at snack time. We cuddled on the couch and she read me Pickle the cat.
entries.highlight: Got a big hug from Mom at preschool pickup and shared that she had not cried at snack time.

entries.title: Snickerdoodles at grandma's
entries.body: Grandma makes snickerdoodles. That's a funny word. Snickerdoodle. Grandma let me roll the balls in the cinnamon sugar. My hands got sparkly sugar. I ate three cookies and grandma didn't tell mommy.
entries.highlight: Rolled snickerdoodle dough in cinnamon sugar with Grandma and enjoyed saying the funny word.

entries.title: Valentine cards for everybody
entries.body: I colored valentines for all my friends. Ava and Mia and Zoe and Ben. I made hearts on all of them. Mommy wrote the names and I did the S at the bottom for Sunny. My S is a little wiggly.
entries.highlight: Colored valentines for her preschool friends and signed each with the letter S.

entries.title: Valentine French toast
entries.body: Yesterday was valentines and I got a heart lollipop from Ben. Today mommy made heart French toast and we had a mommy day. We went to the store and got hair clips with hearts. I'm wearing them now.
entries.highlight: Spent a mommy day after Valentine's Day with heart French toast and a trip for heart hair clips.

entries.title: The goat ate my sleeve
entries.body: We went to the petting zoo in the big warm barn. There was bunnies and a goat. The goat tried to eat my sleeve! I was scared and I hided behind daddy. The bunny was soft though. I like bunnies.
entries.highlight: Visited an indoor petting zoo, got scared when a goat nibbled her sleeve, and loved petting a soft bunny.

entries.title: Banana muffins
entries.body: Me and mommy made banana muffins. I squished the bananas with a fork. Squish squish. It looked yucky but it tasted yummy. We gave one to Brett when he got home from school.
entries.highlight: Mashed bananas for muffins while baking with Mom and saved one for Brett.

entries.title: Sparkle galloped to the kitchen
entries.body: I pretended my unicorn horse Sparkle took me everywhere. We galloped to the kitchen and to the bathroom and to Brett's room. Sparkle eats carrots and rainbow cereal. She is invisible but she is real to me.
entries.highlight: Played with her pretend unicorn horse Sparkle, galloping all over the house and feeding her carrots.

entries.title: I painted mommy's nails
entries.body: This morning I painted mommy's nails for a change. I did pink. I got some on her finger skin too. Mommy said it's beautiful and she will wear it to work. She blowed on them like I do.
entries.favorite: Mommy wearing my nails to work
entries.highlight: Painted Mom's nails pink herself for the first time, and Mom promised to wear them to work.

entries.title: Brett's magic coin
entries.body: Tonight Brett did a magic trick. He made a coin go away and then he found it in my ear! I checked my other ear but there was no more money. Brett said a magician never tells.
entries.highlight: Brett showed her a coin magic trick, pulling a coin from her ear.

entries.title: Daddy built the giant fort
entries.body: Daddy helped me build a giant blanket fort with the dining chairs. It had two rooms. One room for me and one room for Sparkle. We brought flashlights inside and made shadow bunnies on the blanket.
entries.highlight: Built a two-room blanket fort with Dad and made shadow bunnies with flashlights.

entries.title: I didn't cry at drop-off
entries.body: Today I didn't cry at preschool! Not even one tear. I gave mommy a hug and a kiss and I waved bye bye at the window. Miss Joy gave me a sticker that says brave. I'm putting it on my bed.
entries.highlight: Said goodbye to Mom at preschool drop-off without crying for the first time and earned a brave sticker.

entries.title: Dirt cups with Brett
entries.body: Brett made dirt cups. That's chocolate pudding with cookie crumbs on top and gummy bears sleeping in the dirt like bears in a cave. I put five bears in mine. It looked so yucky and it was so yummy.
entries.highlight: Made chocolate pudding dirt cups with gummy bears alongside Brett.

entries.title: Watering grandma's plants
entries.body: I helped grandma water her plants by the window. I had the little green can. Grandma said not too much. I did too much on one plant and water went on the floor. We wiped it up with a towel. Grandma said plants get thirsty like me.
entries.highlight: Watered Grandma's houseplants with a small can and helped wipe up a spill.

entries.title: Blue tongue popsicle
entries.body: I had a blue popsicle after preschool even though it's not summer. My tongue went all blue. I showed Brett and he screamed like a monster and ran. Then I chased him with my blue tongue.
entries.favorite: Chasing Brett with my blue tongue
entries.highlight: Ate a blue popsicle, turned her tongue blue, and chased Brett around with it.

entries.title: Pretend soup for grandma
entries.body: I played grandmas and I made grandma pretend soup with blocks. It was carrot and block soup. Grandma ate it with a pretend spoon and said mmm. Then she showed me how real grandmas knit. The yarn is so tangly.
entries.highlight: Served Grandma pretend block soup during a game of grandmas, and Grandma showed her how to knit.

entries.title: I counted to ten bears
entries.body: I counted my gummy bears. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Ten gummy bears. Mommy said you can have three. So I counted to three and ate them. Counting is easy.
entries.highlight: Counted ten gummy bears by herself and then counted out the three she was allowed to eat.

entries.title: A picture of a thousand cats
entries.body: I drawed a picture of a thousand cats. Well it was twelve cats. But it means a thousand. There's a orange one and a stripey one and a black one with a bow. I want a thousand cats when I'm big.
entries.favorite: The black cat with a bow
entries.highlight: Drew twelve cats to represent her dream of having a thousand cats someday.

entries.title: Ice cream on the bench
entries.body: It was warm today! We ate ice cream outside on the bench. I got strawberry with rainbow sprinkles, my favorite. A bird came and looked at my cone. I said no birdie, this is mine. Sunday is the best day. It is kind of my name.
entries.highlight: Ate strawberry ice cream outside on the first warm Sunday and shooed away a curious bird.

entries.title: Nap in my fort
entries.body: I was so tired after preschool because we did the parachute game. So I took a nap in my blanket fort with Sparkle and my fuzzy blanket. I don't take naps but this was a fort nap. That's different.
entries.highlight: Took a rare nap in her blanket fort after an active preschool day.

entries.title: Two more sleeps
entries.body: Two more sleeps until I am five! I made a birthday fort and I counted on my fingers. Five fingers. That's how old I'm gonna be. Brett said five is old. I said not as old as grandma.
entries.highlight: Built a birthday-countdown fort and counted down two sleeps until turning five.

entries.title: Grandma's birthday cookies
entries.body: Grandma made me special birthday cookies with purple frosting. I helped put the sprinkles on. One more sleep! Grandma said when she was five she had a cake with candles made of real candy. I want that.
entries.highlight: Decorated purple birthday cookies with Grandma the day before turning five.

entries.title: My birthday!
entries.body: My birthday! I am five now. I had a unicorn cake with a gold horn and everybody sang to me. Mommy and daddy and Brett and grandma. And my birthday is on Sunday, my best day, because it is kind of my name! I blowed out all the candles in one blow. I am big now.
entries.highlight: Turned five on a Sunday and celebrated with a unicorn cake and her whole family singing.

entries.title: The dragon book chapter
entries.body: Brett read me one chapter of his dragon book. It's a big kid book with only some pictures. The dragon's name is Ember and she is nice. Brett said now that I'm five I can hear big kid books.
entries.highlight: Brett began reading her a chapter book about a dragon named Ember now that she is five.

entries.title: Tag in the backyard
entries.body: The grass is green so we played tag in the backyard. Brett was it and he chased me around the swing. I tagged him by the fence. My shoes got muddy. Mommy said take them off at the door.
entries.highlight: Played tag with Brett in the spring backyard and came in with muddy shoes.

entries.title: My cat puzzle
entries.body: Today I did my birthday puzzle. It's a puzzle of kittens in a basket. It has fifty pieces. Mommy helped me with the edges and I did the kitten faces. One piece was under the couch.
entries.highlight: Finished a fifty-piece kitten puzzle from her birthday with Mom's help on the edges.

entries.title: Finding the S
entries.body: Brett read me more of the dragon book and he let me find all the S letters on the page. I found seven S. S is for Sunny and snake and sparkle. Brett said I'm a letter detective.
entries.highlight: Found seven S letters on a page while Brett read to her and was called a letter detective.

entries.title: Painting eggs at preschool
entries.body: At preschool we painted paper eggs for Easter. I did purple dots and pink stripes. Mia did hers all green like a frog egg. Miss Joy said mine looked like a party. I'm gonna give it to grandma.
entries.highlight: Painted a dotted and striped paper Easter egg at preschool to give to Grandma.

entries.title: Easter chicks
entries.body: Easter! I found eggs in the yard and then we went to the farm. There were baby chicks that were so fluffy and yellow. I held one in my hands and it peeped. The goat was there again. I waved but I didn't go close.
entries.favorite: The chick peeping in my hands
entries.highlight: Held a baby chick at a farm on Easter but kept her distance from the goat.

entries.title: I wrote my whole name
entries.body: At circle time Miss Joy asked who can write their name. I did! S, U, N, N, Y. All by myself on the whiteboard. The Y was a little backwards. Everybody clapped. Ava can write her name too.
entries.highlight: Wrote her full name on the whiteboard by herself for the first time at preschool.

entries.title: A rainbow for grandma
entries.body: I colored a rainbow for grandma because she gave me the birthday cookies. I used every crayon in the box. Even the brown one, at the bottom. Mommy said grandma will put it on her fridge.
entries.highlight: Colored a rainbow picture for Grandma as a thank-you for her birthday cookies.

entries.title: Ice cream with Ava
entries.body: After preschool Ava's mommy took us for ice cream. Ava got pink and I got strawberry with rainbow sprinkles. We clinked our cones like cheers. Ava is my best friend. We are gonna get married to unicorns.
entries.highlight: Got ice cream with best friend Ava after preschool and toasted with their cones.

entries.title: Unbirthday cake
entries.body: Me and mommy baked an unbirthday cake. That's a cake when it's nobody's birthday. I cracked an egg and some shell fell in. Mommy got it out with a spoon. I stirred so fast the flour went poof.
entries.highlight: Baked an unbirthday cake with Mom and cracked her first egg.

entries.title: A bad dream
entries.body: Yesternight I had a bad dream about a big dog. I went to mommy's bed and she cuddled me. She said dreams are just pictures in our heads. Then I dreamed about Sparkle instead. That was better.
entries.highlight: Woke from a bad dream and was comforted by Mom, then dreamed about her unicorn instead.

entries.title: I read the pictures
entries.body: Brett read me Pickle the cat again and then I read it back to him. I don't know all the words so I read the pictures. Pickle went to the store and got lost and then found. Brett said that's close enough.
entries.highlight: Retold a favorite picture book to Brett by reading the pictures.

entries.title: Story time on the carpet
entries.body: Mommy took me to library story time. I sat on the carpet with the big kids and mommy sat in the back. I didn't need to sit on her lap. The story was about a duck who couldn't swim. He learned.
entries.highlight: Sat on her own at library story time while Mom waited at the back.

entries.title: A secret card
entries.body: I made a secret card for mommy for Mother's Day. Brett helped me hide it under my bed. I drawed me and mommy holding hands with a big sun. Shh, don't tell mommy. It's a surprise.
entries.highlight: Secretly made a Mother's Day card with Brett's help and hid it under her bed.

entries.title: Yellow popsicle on the porch
entries.body: After dinner I had a yellow popsicle on the porch. It's lemon. It was drippy so it went down my arm to my elbow. Brett said I look like a sticky monster. Then I had a bath.
entries.highlight: Ate a drippy lemon popsicle on the porch on a warm evening.

entries.title: Mother's Day breakfast
entries.body: Happy Mother's Day! I gave mommy my secret card and she cried happy tears. Daddy and me made her toast in bed and I put on the jam. Then we colored together all morning. It's Sunday so it's double special.
entries.highlight: Gave Mom her secret Mother's Day card and made her toast in bed with Dad.

entries.title: Rainy cuddle afternoon
entries.body: It rained all day so me and mommy cuddled under the fuzzy blanket. We listened to the rain on the window. Pitter patter. Mommy told me a story about a girl named Sunny who could talk to cats.
entries.favorite: The story about Sunny and the cats
entries.highlight: Cuddled with Mom on a rainy afternoon while Mom made up a story about her.

entries.title: Real worms and gummy bears
entries.body: I found real worms in the garden after the rain. They were pink and slimy and wiggly. Then mommy gave me gummy bears. I said the bears are for eating. The real worms are for the dirt. Don't mix them up.
entries.highlight: Found real earthworms in the garden and then enjoyed gummy bears, carefully telling them apart.

entries.title: Planting flowers with grandma
entries.body: I helped grandma plant flowers in her garden. I digged the holes with the little shovel because grandma's back hurts when she bends. She put the flowers in and I patted the dirt. Pat pat pat. They're pink.
entries.highlight: Dug holes for Grandma's spring flowers since bending hurts Grandma's back.

entries.title: Laying in the grass
entries.body: After preschool I just layed in the grass in the backyard. I looked at the clouds. One cloud looked like a cat and one looked like an ice cream cone. I didn't want to do anything else. My back got itchy.
entries.highlight: Rested in the backyard grass after preschool and found shapes in the clouds.

entries.title: Sour bears
entries.body: Tonight Brett gave me sour gummy bears. My face went all scrunchy. Brett laughed. I said they are too sour but I ate four more. Sour and then sweet. That's a tricky candy.
entries.highlight: Tried sour gummy bears from Brett and made a scrunched-up face but kept eating them.

entries.title: Summer toes
entries.body: Mommy painted my toenails for sandal time. She did light purple. My toes are tickly so I kept wiggling. Mommy said hold still little wiggle worm. Now I can wear my sandals with the flowers.
entries.highlight: Mom painted her toenails light purple so she could wear her flower sandals.

entries.title: Lunch from my play kitchen
entries.body: Grandma came for dinner and after I played grandmas with her. I made her lunch in my play kitchen. A plastic egg and a wooden cookie. She said she's full. I wore her cardigan and it went to my knees.
entries.highlight: Served Grandma pretend food from her play kitchen while wearing Grandma's cardigan.

entries.title: Tag at the park
entries.body: We went to the big park and played tag with Brett and his friend. They're so fast. I hided in the tunnel slide and Brett couldn't find me. Then I jumped out and tagged him. Ha!
entries.highlight: Played tag at the park with Brett and his friend and surprised Brett from the tunnel slide.

entries.title: Ember found her family
entries.body: Brett finished the dragon book! Ember the dragon found her family on the mountain. I was happy and a little sad because the book is over. Brett said there's a book two. I said read it right now. He said tomorrow, Sunny Bunny.
entries.highlight: Brett finished reading the dragon book to her, and she begged to start the sequel right away.

entries.title: A stable for Sparkle
entries.body: I made a stable for Sparkle out of the big box from our new fridge. I drawed hay on the inside and a door with a heart. Sparkle sleeps in it now. She is invisible so she fits.
entries.highlight: Turned a cardboard box into a stable for her pretend unicorn Sparkle.

entries.title: Strawberry shortcake
entries.body: Me and mommy made strawberry shortcake. I washed the strawberries in the sink and mommy cut them. I put the whipped cream on with the squirty can. Squirt! Too much. I ate the extra off my finger.
entries.highlight: Made strawberry shortcake with Mom and was in charge of the whipped cream.

entries.title: The big twisty slide
entries.body: Today on the preschool playground I went down the big twisty slide! I was always scared of it because it's so tall and dark inside. But Ben went first and then me. Whoosh! I want to do it a hundred more times.
entries.highlight: Went down the tall twisty slide on the preschool playground for the first time after Ben went first.

entries.title: Celebration ice cream
entries.body: After pickup mommy said I get celebration ice cream because of the big twisty slide. I got strawberry with rainbow sprinkles. Brett got his chocolate. Daddy got vanilla. Vanilla is boring daddy. He said boring is good.
entries.highlight: Got celebration ice cream with her family for going down the big slide.

entries.title: Brett's noodle dance
entries.body: Brett did a noodle dance because it's almost summer. He wiggled his arms like spaghetti noodles. Pasghetti noodles. I did it too. Then mommy did it and Brett said mom stop. That was the funniest part.
entries.highlight: Joined Brett in a silly noodle dance to celebrate the start of summer.

entries.title: Rain and a movie
entries.body: It rained so I stayed inside. I watched the unicorn movie again with my popcorn bowl. Sparkle the stuffie sat on my lap. I know all the words to the song. I sang it loud.
entries.highlight: Spent a rainy day watching her favorite unicorn movie and singing along.

entries.title: Last day of preschool
entries.body: Last day of preschool! I gave Miss Joy a big hug and a flower picture. She said she will miss me. I'm a little sad. Brett came to pickup and said next year you are in kindergarten like a big kid. I'm going to be so big.
entries.highlight: Said goodbye to Miss Joy on the last day of preschool with a hug and a flower drawing.

entries.title: Rainbow popsicle
entries.body: I had a rainbow popsicle in the backyard. It goes red, then orange, then yellow. I licked it to see the colors. My tongue was all the colors mixed. Brett said it's brown. It's not brown, it's rainbow.
entries.highlight: Ate a rainbow popsicle in the backyard and watched each color appear.

entries.title: I rode my scooter!
entries.body: I rode my scooter all by myself to the end of the street! Nobody held the handle. I pushed with my foot and went and went. I was a little wobbly at the mailbox but I didn't fall. Mommy clapped so loud. I'm a big girl.
entries.highlight: Rode her scooter to the end of the street completely on her own for the first time while Mom cheered.

entries.title: My legs are tired
entries.body: My legs are tired from scootering all weekend. So today was a lay down day. I layed on the couch and mommy brought me apple juice. I said I'm resting my scooter legs. Tomorrow I'm going again.
entries.highlight: Took a lazy day to rest her legs after a weekend of riding her scooter.

entries.title: Lemonade on grandma's porch
entries.body: Grandma made lemonade and cookies and we sat on her porch swing. We swinged slow because of her back. She told me she had a pony when she was little named Buttons. A real pony! I told her about Sparkle.
entries.highlight: Shared lemonade and cookies on Grandma's porch swing and heard about Grandma's childhood pony.

entries.title: Movie theater bears
entries.body: We went to the movie theater! It was so dark and the screen was giant. I had gummy bears in a box and I shared with Brett. I got a little scared when the music was loud but I held daddy's hand.
entries.highlight: Went to the movie theater, shared gummy bears with Brett, and held Dad's hand during loud parts.

entries.title: Chalk cats on the driveway
entries.body: I colored the whole driveway with chalk. I made cats. Lots of cats with whiskers. And a sun with sunglasses. Then daddy drove the car over them and I said daddy, the cats! He said they're okay.
entries.highlight: Covered the driveway in chalk cats and a sun wearing sunglasses.

entries.title: Pool day with mommy
entries.body: Me and mommy went to the big outside pool. I wore my swim vest and my pink swimsuit with the cats on it. Mommy held me and we bounced in the water. I splashed her and she splashed me back. I'm scared to put my face in. Maybe next time.
entries.favorite: Bouncing in the water with mommy
entries.highlight: Spent a pool day with Mom wearing her swim vest, though she was still afraid to put her face in the water.

entries.title: Sorting the bear colors
entries.body: After the pool I sorted my gummy bears by colors on a plate. Red and green bears. Orange and yellow bears. Then I ate the yellow ones first because they are the least best. I saved the red ones for last because they are the best best.
entries.favorite: Saving the red ones for last
entries.highlight: Sorted her gummy bears by color and ate them in order of favorite.

entries.title: Flags for grandma's porch
entries.body: I helped grandma put little flags on her porch for the Fourth of July. I pushed them in the flower pots. Grandma said there's fireworks tomorrow. I don't like fireworks because they go boom. Grandma said I can sit on her lap and she will cover my ears.
entries.highlight: Decorated Grandma's porch with flags and shared that she feels nervous about loud fireworks.

entries.title: Too many booms
entries.body: On the Fourth of July the fireworks were so loud I cried a little. Grandma covered my ears and I watched the sparkly ones. The pink ones were pretty. Today is Sunday and it's quiet so I'm resting. Quiet is better than boom.
entries.highlight: Cried a little at the loud fireworks but liked the pink ones from Grandma's lap, then rested on a quiet Sunday.

entries.title: Old Maid with grandma
entries.body: At grandma's house we played grandmas and then real cards. Grandma taught me Old Maid. You match pairs and nobody wants the old maid card. Grandma said she is the real old lady so the card is scared of her. I got four pairs and grandma got three. I won! I think she let me.
entries.highlight: Learned to play Old Maid with Grandma and won the game.

entries.title: Blueberry picking muffins
entries.body: This morning we picked blueberries at the farm. I ate more than I picked. Then me and mommy made blueberry muffins. I dropped the berries in one by one. Plop, plop. Our muffins are purple inside. Purple is my color.
entries.highlight: Picked blueberries with Mom and baked blueberry muffins that came out purple inside.

entries.title: The cat detective book
entries.body: Tonight Brett started a new book about a cat detective named Inspector Whiskers. He solves mysteries. Brett lets me find words I know. I found the word cat and the word sun! I can read sun because it's in my name.
entries.highlight: Brett started a cat detective book with her, and she recognized the words cat and sun.

entries.title: Splash pad popsicle
entries.body: We went to the splash pad with Zoe. The water comes out of the ground like a surprise. I got so wet. After, Zoe's mommy gave us blue popsicles and we ate them dripping in our towels. Blue drips and water drips.
entries.highlight: Played at the splash pad with Zoe and shared blue popsicles afterward.

entries.title: Star sticker nails
entries.body: Mommy painted my nails light blue and then she put tiny star stickers on top. Like the night sky on my fingers. I kept looking at them all day. At the store a lady said I love your nails and I said my mommy did them.
entries.highlight: Mom gave her a light blue manicure with tiny star stickers, and a stranger complimented it.

entries.title: Water gun tag
entries.body: Me and Brett played tag with water guns. If you get squirted you're it. Brett got me in the back and I screamed because it was cold. Then I got him right in the face. Brett said not the face! I said yes the face.
entries.highlight: Played water gun tag with Brett in the summer heat and scored a direct hit.

entries.title: Fort Sunny summer edition
entries.body: It's too hot outside so I made Fort Sunny inside by the fan. The fan makes the blanket go up and down like breathing. Brett said it's a living fort. I brought my coloring books and two juice boxes. The password is still gummy bear.
entries.highlight: Built her blanket fort by the fan on a hot day, and Brett called it a living fort.

entries.title: Puffball's bunny mansion
entries.body: I want a bunny so bad. She's going to be named Puffball and she's going to be fluffy and white. She will have a bunny mansion with a carrot garden and a slide and a bed with a crown. Mommy said maybe when you're bigger. I'm already bigger.
entries.highlight: Described her dream bunny named Puffball and the bunny mansion she would live in.

entries.title: Sunday spa day
entries.body: Today was a spa day with mommy. We put cucumbers on our eyes and laid on the bed. Then mommy painted both of our nails coral. Matching! It's Sunday so we did everything slow. Mommy said Sunday is our day, and I said because it's kind of my name.
entries.highlight: Had a Sunday spa day with Mom with cucumber eye masks and matching coral nails.

entries.title: Sprinkler then towels
entries.body: I ran through the sprinkler for a long time. Back and forth and back and forth. Then I was so tired I laid in my towel on the deck like a burrito. Mommy called me a Sunny burrito. I almost fell asleep in the sun.
entries.highlight: Ran through the sprinkler and then rested on the deck wrapped in a towel.

entries.title: Sleeping in the fort with Brett
entries.body: Me and Brett camped out in the blanket fort in the living room. We brought sleeping bags. Brett told a story with the flashlight under his chin. It was a little bit scary but then the monster just wanted a cookie. I fell asleep first.
entries.favorite: The monster just wanted a cookie
entries.highlight: Camped out overnight in the blanket fort with Brett, who told a not-so-scary flashlight story.

entries.title: Drawing my whole family
entries.body: I drew my whole family on a big paper. Mommy with long hair, daddy with glasses, Brett with his soccer ball, grandma with her cane, and me in the middle. And Sparkle at the side. And Puffball even though we don't have her yet. I wrote my name at the top.
entries.highlight: Drew a picture of her whole family, adding Sparkle and her wished-for bunny, and signed her name.

entries.title: Picking grandma's tomatoes
entries.body: I helped grandma pick tomatoes in her garden. The little ones are called cherry tomatoes but they're not cherries. I put them in the basket. I picked a green one by mistake and grandma said that one's not ready, like you're not ready to drive. I laughed.
entries.highlight: Harvested cherry tomatoes in Grandma's garden and laughed at Grandma's joke about unripe tomatoes.

entries.title: The fork cookies
entries.body: Grandma made peanut butter cookies. You squish them with a fork to make a criss cross. I did the criss cross on every cookie. Some are criss cross criss cross because I did it twice. Grandma said those are extra special. I took some home for Brett.
entries.highlight: Pressed fork marks into peanut butter cookies at Grandma's and saved some for Brett.

entries.title: I set grandma's table
entries.body: Grandma came for Sunday lunch and I set the table all by myself. Fork on the left, that's the side with the L. I folded the napkins in triangles. I gave grandma the chair with the soft pillow because of her back. She said I'm a good helper.
entries.highlight: Set the table for Sunday lunch by herself and saved the cushioned chair for Grandma.

entries.title: My kindergarten backpack
entries.body: Mommy took me shopping for kindergarten. I picked a purple backpack with a cat on it. The cat has sparkly eyes. And I got a lunchbox and new crayons with sharp points. I wore my backpack around the house all afternoon. It's empty but I like it.
entries.highlight: Shopped with Mom for kindergarten supplies and chose a purple cat backpack.

entries.title: Real lions at the zoo
entries.body: We went to the zoo! I saw real lions and the daddy lion did a big roar. I held mommy's hand tight. Lions are just big cats, so I like them. My favorite was the red panda because he was sleeping in a tree like a fluffy pillow.
entries.highlight: Visited the zoo, heard a lion roar, and fell for a red panda napping in a tree.

entries.title: Racing Brett's bike
entries.body: Brett rode his bike and I rode my scooter next to him on the sidewalk. He went slow so I could keep up. We raced to the stop sign and I won. Brett said I let you win. I said no you didn't. Maybe he did.
entries.highlight: Rode her scooter alongside Brett's bike and raced him to the stop sign.

entries.title: I put my face in the water
entries.body: At the pool I finally put my face in the water! Mommy counted one, two, three and I held my breath and went under. I opened my eyes and saw mommy's legs all blurry. When I came up I was coughing but laughing. Last time I was too scared. Not anymore.
entries.highlight: Put her face under the water at the pool for the first time after being afraid earlier in the summer.

entries.title: Bunny ears with grandma
entries.body: Grandma tried to teach me to tie my shoes. You make bunny ears and cross them and go through the hole. My bunny ears kept falling down. Grandma said practice makes better. I'm going to practice on my teddy bear's shoes. He has no shoes. I'll use a string.
entries.highlight: Started learning to tie her shoes with Grandma's bunny ears method but needs more practice.

entries.title: Tummy butterflies
entries.body: I told mommy my tummy has butterflies about kindergarten. What if I cry like at preschool? Mommy kissed my hand in the middle and said when you miss me, put your hand on your cheek. I tried it. It works. It's Sunday so we just snuggled after.
entries.highlight: Shared her nerves about starting kindergarten, and Mom gave her a kiss in her palm to hold onto.

entries.title: Meeting Mrs. Lee
entries.body: Mommy took me to meet my kindergarten teacher. Her name is Mrs. Lee and she has curly hair and a cat on her mug. A cat! I knew she was nice. I found my cubby with my name on it and Mia is in my class too. Ava is in the other class. That part is sad.
entries.highlight: Met her kindergarten teacher Mrs. Lee at the open house and found her cubby, learning Mia is in her class but Ava is not.

entries.title: Grandma's lucky ribbon
entries.body: Grandma gave me a purple ribbon for my hair. She said she wore it on her first day of school a long, long time ago when dinosaurs were alive. Just kidding, she said. She tied it in a bow on my ponytail. I'm going to wear it for kindergarten so I'm lucky.
entries.highlight: Received Grandma's old purple hair ribbon to wear for luck on the first day of kindergarten.

entries.title: Practice walk to school
entries.body: Mommy and me practiced walking to my new school. It's past the yellow house and the dog that barks and then left at the big tree. I counted the steps but I lost count at sixty-something. I wore my cat backpack for practice. Mommy said I walk like a kindergartner already.
entries.highlight: Practiced the walk to her new school with Mom while wearing her new backpack.

entries.title: Brett's big kid tips
entries.body: Brett gave me big kid tips for kindergarten. Number one, be nice to the lunch lady. Number two, don't eat the glue. Number three, if you're sad, think about something funny, like his frog face. He did the frog face and I laughed. Brett is going into sixth grade. That's really big.
entries.highlight: Brett shared his top tips for kindergarten, including thinking of his frog face when she feels sad.

entries.title: Ducks at the pond
entries.body: In the evening we fed the ducks at the pond with frozen peas, because bread is bad for ducks. The mama duck had five babies following her in a line. I quacked at them and one quacked back! I think she was saying good luck at school tomorrow. Well, the day after tomorrow.
entries.highlight: Fed peas to a mother duck and her ducklings at the pond on the evening before school started.

entries.title: First day of kindergarten
entries.body: First day of kindergarten! I wore grandma's ribbon and my cat backpack. My tummy had butterflies and my eyes got a little wet at the door. But I put my hand on my cheek like mommy said and I was brave. Then Mrs. Lee let us paint and I painted a sun with a smile. I didn't cry really.
entries.highlight: Started kindergarten with Mrs. Lee, felt nervous at the door, and used Mom's hand-kiss trick to be brave.

entries.title: Telling grandma everything
entries.body: Grandma called on the phone to ask about kindergarten. I told her everything. The cubbies, the painting, the slide, and that Ben is in my class too, so that's Mia and Ben. She said did the ribbon work? I said yes it did, I only almost cried. Grandma said that's the bravest kind.
entries.highlight: Told Grandma all about her first day of kindergarten over the phone and credited the lucky ribbon.

entries.title: Worms at the big lunch table
entries.body: In kindergarten we eat lunch in the cafeteria with the big kids. It's so loud. Mommy put gummy bears in my lunchbox and I shared with Mia. I was nice to the lunch lady like Brett said. Her name is Miss Pat and she gave me a high five.
entries.highlight: Ate her first cafeteria lunch, shared gummy bears with Mia, and followed Brett's advice about the lunch lady.

entries.title: Farmers market honey stick
entries.body: Me and mommy went to the farmers market on Saturday morning. A man gave me a honey stick and you bite the end and suck out the honey. It was so sticky. We bought peaches and flowers for the kitchen. Mommy let me pay the lady with the dollar.
entries.highlight: Visited the farmers market with Mom, tried a honey stick, and paid a vendor herself.

entries.title: Apples with caramel dip
entries.body: After school I had apple slices with caramel dip. Mommy said it's a fall snack. I dipped so much that the apple was hiding. Then I told mommy about my day. We have a reading corner with a rug shaped like a turtle. I sat on the turtle's head.
entries.highlight: Had apple slices with caramel after school and described the turtle rug in her classroom.

entries.title: Sight words at the table
entries.body: I have sight word homework. The words are the, and, I, see. Mommy put them on cards on the kitchen table and I had to slap the right one. I slapped see so hard the cards flew. Mommy laughed. I know all four now. I see the cat. That's a whole sentence.
entries.highlight: Practiced her first kindergarten sight words with Mom through a card-slapping game and learned all four.

entries.title: I sounded out C-A-T
entries.body: Today I sounded out a word by myself! Mrs. Lee pointed and I said ccc, aaa, ttt. Cat! I read the word cat with no help. My favorite animal and my first word. Mrs. Lee gave me a cat sticker which is perfect. I told mommy the second she picked me up.
entries.highlight: Sounded out her first word, cat, on her own in kindergarten.

entries.title: Two braids like grandma
entries.body: Mommy did two braids in my hair this morning. She said grandma used to do the same braids for her when she was little. I looked in the mirror and I looked like a picture of mommy. At school Mia said I look like a farmer. A pretty farmer.
entries.favorite: Looking like a picture of mommy
entries.highlight: Mom braided her hair the same way Grandma once did for Mom.

entries.title: Horses at the apple orchard
entries.body: On Sunday we went to the apple orchard and they had horses by the fence. A white one looked just like Sparkle but without a horn. I gave him an apple on my flat hand like daddy showed me. His lips were tickly and wet. I named him Sparkle Two.
entries.highlight: Fed an apple to a white horse at the orchard using a flat hand and named it Sparkle Two.

entries.title: Pumpkin bread
entries.body: Mommy and me made pumpkin bread because it's October. The pumpkin comes in a can which is weird. I measured the cinnamon with the little spoon and leveled it with my finger like a real baker. The whole house smells like fall now. Brett ate two slices.
entries.highlight: Baked pumpkin bread with Mom and carefully measured the cinnamon herself.

entries.title: Grocery helper for grandma
entries.body: Grandma's back was hurting so me and mommy brought her groceries. I carried the light bag all the way to her kitchen and I put the cans in the low cupboard where she can't bend. Then I made her a card and wrote I LOVE YOU by myself. I sounded out love. Grandma hung it on her lamp.
entries.highlight: Carried groceries for Grandma, stocked her low cupboard, and wrote I love you on a card by sounding out the words.

entries.title: Laying in the leaf pile
entries.body: Daddy raked a big leaf pile and I jumped in it a hundred times. Then I just laid there in the leaves looking at the sky. It smelled crunchy. Is crunchy a smell? It is for leaves. It's Sunday, which is sort of my name, so nobody rushed me. I had leaves in my hair at dinner.
entries.highlight: Jumped in and then lay in Dad's leaf pile on a slow Sunday.

entries.title: Rainy Monday cocoa
entries.body: It rained all day and at recess we had to stay inside. After school I was grumpy so mommy made cocoa with tiny marshmallows. I sat by the window in my blanket and watched the rain race down the glass. I picked a raindrop and it won. Then I wasn't grumpy anymore.
entries.highlight: Shook off a grumpy rainy Monday with cocoa and raindrop races at the window.

entries.title: Holding grandma's hand
entries.body: Grandma picked me up from school today. She walks slow with her cane so I walked slow too. At the crosswalk I held her hand and said look both ways grandma. She said yes ma'am. I told her the crossing guard's name is Mr. Bob. Grandma said she knows everything now.
entries.highlight: Walked home slowly with Grandma after school and held her hand at the crosswalk.

entries.title: Brett and the B homework
entries.body: Brett helped me with my homework. I had to draw things that start with B. I drew a ball and a bunny and a banana. Brett said draw Brett, that starts with B. So I drew him with a big nose. He said hey. Then he drew me and gave me a bigger nose.
entries.favorite: Drawing Brett with a big nose
entries.highlight: Brett helped with her letter B homework, and they drew silly pictures of each other.

entries.title: Finger knitting
entries.body: Grandma's hands get sore from knitting so she taught me finger knitting. You use your fingers instead of the sticks. Over, under, pull. I made a long purple worm of yarn. Grandma said that's a scarf for Sparkle. I told her Sparkle says thank you.
entries.highlight: Learned finger knitting from Grandma and made a long yarn scarf for her pretend unicorn.

entries.title: The sheep liked me
entries.body: At the pumpkin patch there was a little farm. I fed a sheep from the cup and her tongue was rough like a cat tongue. There was a goat too. Goats are still too nibbly for me. I remember the one that ate my sleeve. I waved at him from the fence instead.
entries.highlight: Fed a sheep at the pumpkin patch farm but still kept away from the goats after last year's sleeve incident.

entries.title: I tied my shoes by myself
entries.body: I tied my shoes! All by myself! Bunny ears, cross them over, go through the hole and pull. I practiced on my string every night since grandma showed me. Mommy saw and she screamed happy. Then I untied it and did it again to show her it wasn't luck. We called grandma.
entries.favorite: Doing it twice so it wasn't luck
entries.highlight: Tied her own shoes for the first time after weeks of practicing Grandma's bunny ears method.

entries.title: Gummy eyeballs
entries.body: Mommy got Halloween gummy candy. There are gummy eyeballs and gummy bears in orange and black. The eyeballs look at you. I bit one and it was squishy inside. Brett said that's what real eyeballs feel like. Gross Brett. I ate two more.
entries.highlight: Tried spooky Halloween gummy eyeballs and laughed at Brett's gross joke.

entries.title: Picking a kitty costume
entries.body: Me and mommy went to the costume store. There were scary masks so I covered my eyes. I picked a kitty costume with ears and a fluffy tail. Black with a pink nose. Mommy is going to draw whiskers on my face. A thousand cats and I'm one of them.
entries.highlight: Chose a black kitty Halloween costume with Mom at the costume store.

entries.title: Feeding Bubbles the class turtle
entries.body: In my class we have a turtle named Bubbles. This week I'm the turtle feeder! You only do a tiny pinch of pellets because too much is bad for him. Bubbles swam up to the top and snapped them up. Mrs. Lee said I did a perfect pinch. Bubbles is green like a pickle.
entries.highlight: Took a turn as the class turtle feeder in kindergarten and carefully gave the right amount of food.

entries.title: Pumpkin guts
entries.body: We carved pumpkins! Mommy cut the top off and I scooped out the guts with my hands. It was slimy and cold and stringy. Ew, ew, ew. But kind of fun. My pumpkin has triangle eyes and a smile with one tooth. Mommy roasted the seeds and they were salty.
entries.highlight: Scooped pumpkin seeds with her bare hands and designed a one-toothed jack-o-lantern with Mom.

entries.title: Grandma fixed my tail
entries.body: My kitty tail fell off when I tried my costume on. I was so sad. Grandma said bring it here and she sewed it back on with a needle. I held the thread for her because her eyes are tired and I threaded the needle. Well, I tried. Grandma did the last part.
entries.highlight: Brought her broken costume tail to Grandma, who sewed it back on while she helped hold the thread.

entries.title: Practicing trick or treat
entries.body: Brett is going to be a zombie and he practiced his zombie walk. Then we practiced trick or treat at my bedroom door. I knocked and said trick or treat and Brett gave me a sock. A sock! I said that's not candy. He said happy Halloween, it's a sock treat.
entries.highlight: Practiced trick-or-treating with Brett, who handed her a sock as a joke.

entries.title: Halloween kitty
entries.body: I was a kitty for Halloween with a black tail and pink nose and mommy drew whiskers. Brett was a zombie and he held my bucket when it got too heavy. I said meow at every door. One lady said what a cute kitty and gave me two. I didn't get scared of the spooky house, I just held Brett's hand.
entries.highlight: Trick-or-treated as a kitty while zombie Brett carried her heavy bucket and held her hand at the spooky house.

entries.title: Sorting my candy
entries.body: After trick or treating I dumped all my candy on the carpet and sorted it. Chocolate pile, gummy pile, and yucky pile. The yucky pile is for daddy. I counted twenty-two gummy things. Mommy said I can have two tonight. I picked a gummy bear and a lollipop, and then I took off my kitty ears.
entries.highlight: Sorted and counted her Halloween candy and chose two treats for the night.

entries.title: Candy trades with Brett
entries.body: On Sunday me and Brett did candy trades. I gave him my peanut ones because I don't like peanuts. He gave me his gummy bears. Then he tried to trade one tiny raisin box for my big lollipop. I said no way José. Brett said who is José. I don't know.
entries.highlight: Traded Halloween candy with Brett and refused his sneaky raisin-for-lollipop offer.

entries.title: Dark at dinnertime
entries.body: The clocks changed and now it's dark at dinner. Mommy and me went outside after dinner and looked at the stars. She showed me the Big Dipper. It looks like a pot for soup. I said one star is winking at me. Mommy said that's an airplane. Oh.
entries.highlight: Stargazed with Mom after the time change and mistook an airplane for a winking star.

entries.title: What Mrs. Lee told mommy
entries.body: Mommy went to talk to Mrs. Lee at the parent meeting. When she came home she said Mrs. Lee said I'm very kind and I help kids who are sad. And I'm learning to read so fast. Mommy gave me the biggest hug. I felt proud and shy at the same time. Is that a feeling?
entries.favorite: Proud and shy at the same time
entries.highlight: Heard from Mom that Mrs. Lee praised her kindness and reading progress at the parent-teacher conference.

entries.title: Grandma's birthday card
entries.body: Tomorrow is grandma's birthday so I made her a card tonight. I wrote HAPPY BIRTHDAY GRANDMA. Mommy spelled birthday because it's long, but I did happy and grandma by myself. I drew her with a crown because she's the queen of cookies. And I drew Buttons the pony.
entries.highlight: Made Grandma a birthday card, writing most of the words herself and drawing Grandma's childhood pony.

entries.title: Star student sprinkles
entries.body: I was star student of the week! I got to bring my favorite thing to show the class and I brought Sparkle the stuffie. So daddy took me for strawberry ice cream with rainbow sprinkles after school even though it's cold. He tried strawberry this time. He said okay, strawberry is not boring.
entries.favorite: Daddy said strawberry is not boring
entries.highlight: Celebrated being star student of the week with strawberry ice cream, and Dad finally tried her flavor.

entries.title: Friday fort movie night
entries.body: Friday movie night! I made a fort around the couch and we watched a movie about a lost puppy. Mommy and daddy and Brett and me all squished in. Brett's feet were in my face. At the sad part I hid in my blanket. The puppy found his home so it was okay.
entries.highlight: Hosted a Friday movie night in a couch fort with the whole family.

entries.title: Pie crust with grandma
entries.body: I went to grandma's to get ready for Thanksgiving. Grandma said her hands are too stiff today so I rolled the pie crust with the rolling pin. She told me how. I also wrote name cards for everybody at the table. Mommy, daddy, Brett, grandma, me. I sounded them all out. Grandma said I'm her right hand.
entries.highlight: Rolled out the Thanksgiving pie crust for Grandma and wrote every family member's name card by sounding them out.

entries.title: My turkey hand
entries.body: At school we made turkeys from our hands. You trace your hand and the fingers are feathers. I colored mine purple of course. Then we wrote I am thankful for. I wrote my family and cats. Mrs. Lee said how do you spell family, and I did it. F-A-M-L-E. Close enough she said.
entries.highlight: Made a hand turkey in kindergarten and wrote that she is thankful for her family and cats.

entries.title: Peppermint cocoa first snow
entries.body: It snowed today, the first snow! Just a little but it counts. After school mommy made peppermint cocoa with a candy cane stirring stick. You stir and the candy cane melts a little. I licked it. Brett says it's going to snow more so we can go sledding. I can't wait.
entries.highlight: Celebrated the first snow of winter with peppermint cocoa after school.

entries.title: Reading to Sparkle in the fort
entries.body: After school I made a small fort under my desk and I read my little school book to Sparkle the stuffie. It's called The Big Red Hat. I know almost all the words. When I got stuck on the word went, I sounded it out, w-e-n-t. Sparkle is a good listener because she never says hurry up.
entries.highlight: Read her kindergarten take-home book aloud to her stuffed unicorn inside a small fort, sounding out tricky words.

entries.title: Gingerbread house at school
entries.body: In class we made gingerbread houses out of graham crackers and frosting. The frosting is like glue but yummy glue. My roof kept sliding off so Mrs. Lee helped me hold it. I put gumdrops on the roof and a gummy bear in the yard like a guard. Ben's house fell down and he laughed.
entries.favorite: The gummy bear guard in the yard
entries.highlight: Built a graham cracker gingerbread house in kindergarten, with Mrs. Lee helping steady the roof.

entries.title: Wrapping grandma's present
entries.body: On Sunday me and mommy wrapped presents. Grandma's present is fuzzy socks with grippy dots on the bottom so she doesn't slip, that was my idea. I cut the paper and it was crooked so we folded it extra. I used so much tape. Mommy said it looks homemade, and that's the best kind.
entries.favorite: The grippy socks were my idea
entries.highlight: Wrapped Grandma's Christmas present with Mom, grippy socks she chose so Grandma would not slip.

entries.title: My line in the sing-along
entries.body: We are practicing for the holiday sing-along and Mrs. Lee picked me to say a line by myself. My line is, and the stars shine bright on everyone. I practiced it in the car and in the bath and to Brett. My voice gets shaky when I think about all the parents. But I know the words.
entries.highlight: Was chosen to say a solo line in the kindergarten holiday sing-along and practiced it everywhere.

entries.title: Down the big hill by myself
entries.body: After school Brett took me to the big sledding hill, not the baby hill. Last year I only went on the little one with him holding me. Today I went down the big hill all by myself on the purple sled! My eyes were watery from the wind. At the bottom Brett yelled Sunny Bunny is a legend. I went seven times.
entries.highlight: Sledded down the big hill alone for the first time, a year after only riding the small hill with Brett.

entries.title: Our snow fort
entries.body: Before school Brett and me started a snow fort in the backyard. He made the walls with a bucket like a sandcastle and I patted the cracks closed. We made a pile of snowballs in case daddy attacks. Daddy attacked when he went out to the car. We won. Then my fingers were numb and mommy said boots off, bus time.
entries.highlight: Built a snow fort with Brett before school and won a snowball fight against Dad.

entries.title: I said my line!
entries.body: Today was the holiday sing-along on the last day before break. I stood on the stage with my class and all the parents were looking. I was scared for one second. Then I said my line really loud. And the stars shine bright on everyone! Mommy and grandma clapped the loudest. I didn't forget a single word.
entries.favorite: Mommy and grandma clapped the loudest
entries.highlight: Spoke her solo line loudly and clearly at the kindergarten holiday sing-along in front of all the families.

entries.title: Real reindeer at the tree farm
entries.body: This morning we went to the tree farm and they had real reindeer in a pen! They are smaller than I thought and they have fuzzy antlers. One was named Dasher, just like Santa's. I fed him a carrot through the fence. I asked if he's going to work tonight and the man said yes, very busy.
entries.favorite: Dasher is going to work tonight
entries.highlight: Fed a carrot to a real reindeer named Dasher at the tree farm on Christmas Eve.

entries.title: My letter to Santa
entries.body: Tonight I wrote Santa a letter all by myself. Dear Santa, I want a bunny named Puffball, please. I know bunnies are hard to keep warm in the sleigh so a toy one is okay too. Love Sunny. Mommy helped me spell please. I put it next to the cookies and the carrot for Dasher.
entries.favorite: A toy one is okay too
entries.highlight: Wrote her own letter to Santa asking for a bunny and kindly allowed for a toy version.

entries.title: Christmas!
entries.body: Christmas! It snowed in the night again. Santa brought a fluffy toy bunny, and she's Puffball, so Santa read my letter. And a book I can read myself about a cat who bakes. Then Brett took me sledding and snowboarding. This year I stood up on the snowboard for three whole seconds before I fell. Brett said last year you sat on it like a sled.
entries.highlight: Received a toy bunny named Puffball and a book she can read herself, then stood up on Brett's snowboard for the first time.

entries.title: Kid midnight
entries.body: Last night we did kid midnight at nine o'clock. We counted down ten, nine, eight, and banged pots with spoons. Then I went to sleep and the grown ups did real midnight. Today I was in pajamas all day, like last New Year. I read my cat baking book to Puffball three times.
entries.highlight: Celebrated an early kid midnight on New Year's Eve and spent New Year's Day in pajamas reading.

entries.title: Putting away the ornaments
entries.body: Me and mommy took down the Christmas tree. I wrapped every ornament in tissue paper like a little blanket so they don't break. The glass ones mommy did. I found the ornament I made in preschool with my handprint. My hand was so small then. Now it's way bigger.
entries.highlight: Helped Mom pack away ornaments and noticed how much bigger her hand is than her preschool handprint ornament.

entries.title: Ice skating with the penguin
entries.body: Mommy took me ice skating at the rink. The ice is so slippery that my legs went in two directions. They have plastic penguins you can push, so I pushed the penguin around and around. By the end I let go for a little bit. Mommy held my mitten. My cheeks got red and cold.
entries.highlight: Went ice skating with Mom for the first time, pushing a penguin helper and letting go briefly at the end.

entries.title: The cardinal in the snow
entries.body: Back to school today. After school I sat at the window with daddy and watched our bird feeder. A red cardinal came and he looked so bright on the white snow. Daddy said the brown one is his wife. I named them Mister and Missus Red. They ate all the sunflower seeds.
entries.highlight: Watched a pair of cardinals at the bird feeder with Dad after the first day back at school.

entries.title: Bunny facts
entries.body: I got a library book all about bunnies. Me and mommy read it together. I learned that when bunnies are happy they jump and twist in the air, and that is called a binky. Their big ears help them stay cool. Some of them weigh less than my backpack! I told mommy that means one would fit in a bunny mansion easy.
entries.highlight: Read a library book about bunnies with Mom and shared facts about her dream bunny.

entries.title: Mommy came to my class
entries.body: Mommy was the mystery reader in my class today! Nobody knew who it was and then she came in the door and I screamed mommy. She read a book about a bear and did the voices like Brett does. Everybody liked her. I sat right in the front on the turtle rug. I felt so proud.
entries.highlight: Mom surprised her class as the mystery reader, and she sat proudly in front.

entries.title: Brett taught me checkers
entries.body: Brett taught me checkers on Sunday. You move on the dark squares and if you jump the other one you take it. When you get to the end you get a king and you stack it. I got two kings! Brett still won but he said I'm getting tricky. Next time I'm gonna win for real.
entries.highlight: Learned to play checkers with Brett and earned two kings even though he won.

entries.title: Pink snow cream
entries.body: Mommy made snow cream! You get clean fresh snow in a bowl and add milk and sugar and vanilla. I asked for pink so she put a drop of red food coloring and rainbow sprinkles. It was strawberry ice cream but made of snow. Not as good as the real one from the shop, but almost. Brett had three bowls.
entries.favorite: Pink ice cream made of snow
entries.highlight: Made pink snow cream with Mom from fresh snow on a Sunday.

entries.title: Snow day reading fort
entries.body: Snow day! No school. I built Fort Sunny with the big couch cushions and brought in all my books. I read three books by myself. I had to sound out some words, like jumped and garden. Mommy brought cocoa to the door and said the password. She still remembered it's gummy bear.
entries.highlight: Spent a snow day reading three books on her own inside Fort Sunny.

entries.title: I read Brett a whole page
entries.body: Tonight Brett was going to read to me but I said wait, I want to read to you. I read a whole page of my cat baking book by myself. The cat mixed the flour and the eggs and made a big mess. I only needed help with one word, which was kitchen. Brett said whoa, you're a real reader now.
entries.highlight: Read an entire page of a book aloud to Brett for the first time, needing help with only one word.

entries.title: A hundred piece puzzle
entries.body: I did a puzzle with one hundred pieces! Last spring I did fifty with mommy's help. This one is cats on a bookshelf. I did the edges first like mommy taught me. It took me all morning and I didn't give up even when the blue pieces all looked the same. Daddy found the last piece in his slipper.
entries.highlight: Completed a one hundred piece cat puzzle mostly on her own, up from fifty pieces with help last spring.

entries.title: Earache day
entries.body: My ear hurt so much so I stayed home from school and went to the doctor. The doctor looked in my ear with a little light. I have an ear infection and I have pink medicine that tastes like bubble gum. I laid on the couch with a warm towel on my ear. Puffball the toy sat with me.
entries.highlight: Stayed home with an ear infection and rested on the couch with warm towels and her toy bunny.

entries.title: Kittens at the pet store
entries.body: We went to the pet store for bird seed and they had kittens from the shelter in a big glass room. There was a gray one with white socks who batted at my finger through the glass. I asked mommy can we take her, just one cat, not a thousand. Mommy said not right now. I said bye kitty. My heart was a little sad.
entries.highlight: Met adoptable kittens at the pet store and felt sad when Mom said they could not take one home.

entries.title: Ava sleeps over in my fort
entries.body: Ava slept over at my house! We made the biggest blanket fort and put our sleeping bags inside. We told secrets and giggled until mommy said girls, sleep. My secret was I'm still scared of the dark a little. Ava said she is too. So we kept the flashlight on low.
entries.favorite: Ava is scared of the dark too
entries.highlight: Had best friend Ava to sleep over in a blanket fort and shared that they are both a little afraid of the dark.

entries.title: A crown of one hundred
entries.body: Soon it's the hundredth day of school and I have to make a crown with a hundred things. Brett helped me glue one hundred stickers on a paper crown. We counted by tens, ten, twenty, thirty, all the way up. Brett said when he was in kindergarten he used one hundred noodles and they all fell off.
entries.highlight: Made a hundredth day crown with Brett, gluing one hundred stickers and counting by tens.

entries.title: I made my own breakfast
entries.body: This morning I made my own breakfast! I got the cereal box down and poured it and only spilled a little bit. Then I poured the milk from the small jug, not the big one. Mommy came down and said who made breakfast? I said me, Sunny the chef. She took a picture.
entries.highlight: Poured her own cereal and milk for breakfast before Mom came downstairs.

entries.title: Salt on grandma's steps
entries.body: Grandma's front steps were icy so me and daddy went over to put salt on them. I sprinkled it like I sprinkle cookies, but daddy said a little more. Grandma watched from the window and waved. I don't want her to slip because her back already hurts. Then she gave us tea and I had mine with lots of honey.
entries.highlight: Helped Dad salt Grandma's icy front steps so Grandma would not slip.

entries.title: The hundredth day snack
entries.body: Today was the hundredth day of school! I wore my sticker crown. We made a snack mix with ten of ten things. Ten pretzels, ten raisins, ten gummy bears, ten crackers, and more. I traded my raisins with Ben for his gummy bears. Mrs. Lee said we are one hundred days smarter.
entries.highlight: Celebrated the hundredth day of kindergarten wearing her sticker crown and counting out a hundred-piece snack mix.

entries.title: Cheering up Brett
entries.body: Brett had a bad day because his soccer team lost and his friend was mean. He was quiet at dinner and he didn't do any silly faces. So after dinner I made him a card that said you are the best brother and I drew his frog face on it. He laughed a little. Then he said thanks Sunny Bunny and he hugged me.
entries.highlight: Noticed Brett was sad after a hard day and made him a card with his own frog face to cheer him up.

entries.title: Valentines for the whole class
entries.body: For Valentine's Day I made cards for my whole class, twenty kids. Last year mommy wrote all the names. This year I wrote every name by myself. That's a lot of writing, my hand got tired. I gave Ava a special one with a unicorn even though she's in the other class. Daddy got mommy flowers and I got a little heart necklace.
entries.highlight: Wrote all twenty classmates' names on her valentines herself, something Mom did for her the year before.

entries.title: Butterflies at the butterfly house
entries.body: On Sunday we went to the butterfly house at the zoo. Inside it was warm like summer even though it's winter. The butterflies were bright purple and blue and they flew around like flying flowers. They taste with their feet! I stood still for a long time and a purple one landed on my sleeve. Brett held out his finger to a big brown one but it flew away.
entries.favorite: The purple butterfly on my sleeve
entries.highlight: Visited the zoo butterfly house on a winter Sunday and stood still until a butterfly landed on her sleeve.

entries.title: My first wiggly tooth came out
entries.body: My first tooth came out! It was wiggly for a whole week and tonight it came out in an apple. There was a little blood but I didn't cry. Mommy put it in a tiny tooth pillow. I can whistle through the hole a little bit. Brett said the tooth fairy pays more for the first one.
entries.highlight: Lost her first baby tooth while biting an apple and stayed calm through it.

entries.title: Grandma and the tooth fairy
entries.body: The tooth fairy gave me a gold coin and some glitter on my windowsill. I showed grandma my hole when she picked me up. Grandma said when she was little the tooth fairy gave her a penny. A penny! I said that's not fair, and grandma laughed so much she had to sit down on the bench.
entries.highlight: Showed Grandma her missing tooth and the tooth fairy's coin, and laughed together about Grandma's penny.

entries.title: A snow unicorn
entries.body: We had more snow so I made a snow unicorn instead of a snowman. It looked more like a snow dog, but I put a carrot on its head for a horn. I named her Snow Sparkle. I don't really play pretend Sparkle every day anymore, but I still like her. Snow Sparkle melted a little in the sun by dinner.
entries.highlight: Built a snow unicorn named Snow Sparkle and reflected that she plays pretend Sparkle less than she used to.

entries.title: I moved to the blue group
entries.body: Today Mrs. Lee moved me up to the blue reading group! The blue group reads the books with more words and not as many pictures. Mia is in blue too. I was nervous I wouldn't know the words but I knew almost all of them. I read the sentence the dog ran up the hill fast.
entries.highlight: Moved up to a higher kindergarten reading group and read longer sentences confidently.

entries.title: Doctor Sunny for Brett
entries.body: Brett has a cold and his nose is all red. I played doctor Sunny. I brought him tissues and a cold washcloth and my stuffed Puffball to keep him company. I took his temperature with my toy thermometer and said you have a hundred fevers. Brett said that's bad. I said rest and drink juice.
entries.highlight: Took care of Brett while he had a cold, bringing tissues and playing doctor.

entries.title: A new grandma game
entries.body: I still play grandmas with grandma but now the game is different. Now I'm the helper and she's the real grandma. I bring her the pretend medicine and the real glasses when she can't find them. Today they were on her head the whole time. I said grandma, they're on your head! She said oh my goodness, what would I do without you.
entries.favorite: The glasses were on her head
entries.highlight: Played a new version of grandmas where she acts as Grandma's helper and found Grandma's glasses on her head.

entries.title: Grandma's skipping song
entries.body: Grandma taught me a song she sang when she was a little girl. It's about a little bird on a fence and you clap in the middle. She sang it slow and I sang it fast. Then we did it together and grandma's voice went wobbly and high. I'm going to teach it to Mia and Zoe at recess.
entries.highlight: Learned a clapping song from Grandma's childhood and planned to teach it to friends.

entries.title: The giant gummy bear experiment
entries.body: At school we did an experiment. We put a gummy bear in water overnight and today it was huge and squishy like a slug. Mrs. Lee said the water went inside it. I wrote my guess first and I guessed it would get bigger, and I was right! I didn't eat it. It was too gross even for me.
entries.highlight: Did a kindergarten science experiment where a gummy bear swelled in water, and her prediction was correct.

entries.title: Cinnamon rolls on a lost-hour Sunday
entries.body: The clocks jumped forward last night so we lost an hour of sleep. Mommy said Sunday is the perfect day to be slow anyway, and I said that's because it's kind of my name. We made cinnamon rolls from scratch. I rolled out the dough and spread the butter and sprinkled the cinnamon sugar all the way to the edges. Then we rolled it up like a sleeping bag and cut it with a string. I didn't know you could cut with a string. They were the best thing I ever baked.
entries.highlight: Baked cinnamon rolls from scratch with Mom on a slow Sunday after the time change and learned to cut dough with string.

entries.title: Caterpillars in our classroom
entries.body: Our class got a box of tiny caterpillars in a cup! They are so small, like little black eyelashes, and they eat brown goo at the bottom. Mrs. Lee said they will turn into butterflies, and we have to be patient. I'm not very good at patient. I drew them in my caterpillar journal and wrote day one, they are wiggly. I named mine Noodle, even though we don't know which one is which.
entries.highlight: Started observing caterpillars in her kindergarten class and recorded the first day in her caterpillar journal.

entries.title: Reading in the eye doctor waiting room
entries.body: I went with grandma and mommy to grandma's eye doctor. In the waiting room grandma didn't have her reading glasses, so I read her the signs. Please check in at the desk. Restroom is down the hall. Then I read her a little bit of a kids magazine about otters. Grandma said she brought her own reader today. It felt good to help her with something I just learned.
entries.highlight: Read the waiting room signs and a magazine aloud to Grandma at her eye appointment.

entries.title: Copying grandma's recipe card
entries.body: Grandma let me copy her snickerdoodle recipe onto my own card. Her card is old and has butter stains and her handwriting is curly. I wrote it in my handwriting, which is not curly yet. Two cups flour, one cup sugar, and the cream of tartar part, which is a funny name. Grandma said now the recipe will live in two kitchens. I'm keeping mine in my desk drawer.
entries.favorite: The recipe will live in two kitchens
entries.highlight: Copied Grandma's snickerdoodle recipe onto her own card in her own handwriting.

entries.title: The leprechaun trap
