entries.body: For Saint Patrick's Day Brett and I built a leprechaun trap out of a shoebox and a ladder made of popsicle sticks. We put gold chocolate coins inside. This morning the trap was empty but there were tiny green footprints on the table and my milk was green! The leprechaun is very tricky. After school I just stayed cozy in green socks and read on the couch.
entries.highlight: Built a leprechaun trap with Brett and woke up to green footprints and green milk on Saint Patrick's Day.

entries.title: I fed the goat!
entries.body: We went back to the farm and I fed a goat! When I was four a goat tried to eat my sleeve and I hid behind daddy, and I've been scared of goats ever since. Today I put the food on my flat hand like with the horses, and I held still even though my heart was beating fast. The goat's lips were soft and he didn't bite me at all. I fed him three more times. I named him Mister Nibbles. I'm not scared of goats anymore.
entries.highlight: Overcame her fear of goats by hand-feeding one at the farm, about a year after a goat nibbled her sleeve.

entries.title: Seeds in egg cartons
entries.body: On Sunday grandma and I planted seeds inside in old egg cartons. Tomatoes and flowers and basil. I put a little dirt in each cup and poked a hole with my pinky and dropped in two seeds. Grandma says they need to stay inside until it's warm. I wrote labels on popsicle sticks so we don't forget which is which. Grandma said my writing is easier to read than hers.
entries.highlight: Started seedlings in egg cartons with Grandma and wrote all the plant labels herself.

entries.title: Talking about Zoe with mommy
entries.body: After school mommy and I took a walk and I told her that Zoe said I'm not her friend anymore because I played with Mia. It made my throat feel tight. Mommy said sometimes friends say things when they feel left out. She asked what I could say. I decided I would tell Zoe that she can play with us both. Talking about it made the tight feeling go away a little. We found a tree with pink buds.
entries.highlight: Talked with Mom on a walk about a hurtful comment from Zoe and came up with a plan to include her.

entries.title: Noodle made a chrysalis
entries.body: Today I asked Zoe to play with me and Mia at recess, like I planned with mommy, and she said okay! We played horses. And in class, the caterpillars climbed to the top of the cup and turned into chrysalises. They hang upside down like little brown sleeping bags. Mrs. Lee said they are changing inside but we can't see it. I think that is a little like me learning to read. You can't see it happening, and then you can just do it.
entries.highlight: Successfully included Zoe at recess and compared the caterpillars forming chrysalises to her own learning.

entries.title: My three-sentence story
entries.body: In writing time I wrote my first story with three whole sentences. It was about Puffball. Puffball is a fluffy bunny. She lives in a bunny mansion. She likes to eat strawberry ice cream. I used finger spaces and periods at the end. Mrs. Lee put it on the wall in the hallway with a gold star. When mommy picked me up I made her come look at it before we left.
entries.favorite: My story is in the hallway
entries.highlight: Wrote her first three-sentence story, about her dream bunny Puffball, and it was displayed in the school hallway.

entries.title: Mommy in grandma's photo album
entries.body: I helped grandma with spring cleaning. I dusted the low shelves where she can't reach without bending. On the bottom shelf I found an old photo album, and inside there was mommy when she was little! She had two braids just like the ones she does for me, and she was missing her front tooth. Grandma told me mommy was scared of the vacuum cleaner. I'm going to tease mommy about it.
entries.favorite: Mommy was scared of the vacuum
entries.highlight: Dusted Grandma's low shelves and discovered childhood photos of Mom with braids and a missing tooth.

entries.title: I read Brett a whole book
entries.body: I read Brett a whole book by myself, every single page! It's a library book called The Snail Who Wanted to Fly. Brett used to read to me every night, and tonight I read to him. He laid on my bed with his hands behind his head like he was the little kid. I only needed help with two words, which were adventure and suddenly. At the end Brett clapped and said that was better than the dragon book. I said that's not true. But I was really proud.
entries.favorite: Brett laid down like the little kid
entries.highlight: Read an entire library book aloud to Brett on her own, reversing their bedtime reading routine.

entries.title: The butterflies came out
entries.body: The butterflies came out of the chrysalises! They're orange with black spots and their wings were crumpled at first, and then they opened them slowly to dry. Mrs. Lee took us outside and we let them go in the school garden. One landed on Ben's shoe and he froze like a statue. I said bye Noodle, even though I don't know which one was Noodle. I was a tiny bit sad but mostly happy for them.
entries.highlight: Watched the class butterflies emerge and helped release them in the school garden.

entries.title: Dyeing eggs the day before Easter
entries.body: Mommy and I dyed Easter eggs at the kitchen table. You put a tablet in vinegar and it fizzes and makes the color. I wrote names on the eggs with the white crayon first, so when you dye them the names show up like magic. I wrote Brett, Daddy, Mommy, Grandma and Sunny. My egg is purple, of course. I dipped one egg half in blue and half in pink, and it came out like a sunset.
entries.favorite: The names showed up like magic
entries.highlight: Dyed Easter eggs with Mom and used a white crayon to write each family member's name on an egg.

entries.title: My birthday!
entries.body: My birthday! I am six now, a whole hand and one more finger. It was on a Monday this year, not a Sunday, but my class sang to me and I got to wear the birthday crown. After school I had a cat cake with whiskers made of licorice, and everybody sang again, mommy, daddy, Brett and grandma. My big present was a purple bike with training wheels and a basket with flowers. I am big now, for real.
entries.favorite: My purple bike with a basket
entries.highlight: Turned six, celebrated at school and at home with a cat cake, and got a purple bike with training wheels.

entries.title: First wobbly bike ride
entries.body: Mommy took me out to ride my new bike. With training wheels it's not supposed to tip, but it still leans and wiggles. Pedaling is harder than scootering because you have to push and steer at the same time. I went down the sidewalk to the yellow house and back. I was scared at the bumpy part, but I kept going. My legs were burning. Mommy said I look like I've been biking forever. I haven't, it's day one.
entries.highlight: Took her first rides on her new bike with training wheels and kept pedaling through a scary bumpy patch.

entries.title: Grandma watched me ride
entries.body: Grandma sat on our porch in the comfy chair with her tea and watched me ride my bike up and down the driveway. Every time I passed I rang my bell, ding ding, and she waved. She said when she was a girl she rode a bike to the store to buy candy for a nickel. I asked if I can ride to the store and she said maybe when you're twelve like Brett. That's forever away.
entries.highlight: Showed Grandma her bike riding while Grandma watched from the porch and told stories about her own childhood bike.

entries.title: Reading grandma the funnies
entries.body: On Sunday I read grandma the comics in her newspaper because her eyes get tired from small words. Some of the jokes I didn't understand, but grandma laughed at them anyway. There was one with a cat who hates Mondays, and I understood that one. Then grandma read me a poem she knows by heart without even looking. I want to know a poem by heart. I'm going to pick one and practice.
entries.highlight: Read the Sunday comics aloud to Grandma, who then recited a poem from memory.

entries.title: Rainy day comic book
entries.body: It rained so hard after school that the gutters made a waterfall. I stayed inside and made my own comic book. I folded paper in half and stapled it. It's called Puffball and the Thousand Cats. Puffball is scared of the cats at first but they all become friends and live in the bunny mansion together. I drew the boxes and wrote the words in bubbles. It has six pages. Brett asked to read it and laughed at the right parts.
entries.favorite: Brett laughed at the right parts
entries.highlight: Wrote and illustrated a six-page comic book about Puffball and a thousand cats on a rainy afternoon.

entries.title: Raking grandma's flower beds
entries.body: After school I raked the old leaves out of grandma's flower beds so the tulips can come up. Grandma pointed and I raked. Underneath the leaves there were little green shoots already poking out. Grandma said they've been waiting all winter. I was careful not to step on them. Last spring I only dug the holes, but this year grandma let me use the real rake, not the little one. My arms are tired but it looks so neat.
entries.favorite: The shoots were waiting all winter
entries.highlight: Raked Grandma's flower beds with a full-size rake, uncovering spring shoots and taking on more of the work than last year.

entries.title: Brett made me goalie
entries.body: Brett has soccer practice tomorrow so he practiced in the backyard and made me be the goalie. The goal is two buckets. He kicked soft ones and I caught four of them! One went right in my tummy and it knocked my breath out a little, and Brett ran over and said are you okay, I'm sorry. I said I'm fine, kick another one. He said I'm tougher than his friends.
entries.highlight: Played goalie for Brett's backyard soccer practice and caught four shots.

entries.title: Earth Day dirt cups
entries.body: It was Earth Day so we picked up trash on the school playground with gloves. I found a bottle cap and a candy wrapper and a sock. Who loses a sock at school? After school Brett and I made dirt cups like we did last year, with chocolate pudding and cookie crumbs and gummy bears. Brett said the gummy bears are napping in the dirt, but the real worms do the work of helping the earth. That's actually true about real worms.
entries.highlight: Helped clean up the school playground for Earth Day and made gummy bear dirt cups with Brett again.

entries.title: I ordered by myself
entries.body: It was warm enough for the ice cream shop. This time I ordered by myself at the counter. I said one strawberry in a cone, please, with rainbow sprinkles. Daddy gave me a five dollar bill and I paid and I counted the change, one dollar and a quarter. The lady said I was very polite. I used to hide behind mommy's leg when people talked to me. Now I just talk.
entries.favorite: I used to hide, now I just talk
entries.highlight: Ordered and paid for her own ice cream and counted the change, noting she used to be too shy to speak to strangers.

entries.title: I painted grandma's nails
entries.body: Grandma came for Sunday lunch, and after lunch I painted her nails. Mommy taught me how. You do three strokes, one in the middle and one on each side. Grandma picked pink like the flowers. Her hands are wrinkly and soft and they shake a little, so I held them gently. I only got a little on her skin. Grandma said she hasn't had her nails done in years. She kept holding them up to look.
entries.favorite: She kept holding them up to look
entries.highlight: Painted Grandma's nails after Sunday lunch using the technique Mom taught her, holding Grandma's hands gently.

entries.title: Our secret notebook
entries.body: Mommy and I started a secret notebook. I write her a note and leave it on her pillow, and she writes back and leaves it on mine. Tonight I wrote, Dear Mommy, thank you for teaching me nails. Grandma loved them. Love Sunny. I drew a heart and a little cat. Mommy wrote back that she was proud of me for being so gentle. I'm keeping the notebook under my pillow so Brett can't read it.
entries.highlight: Started a secret back-and-forth notebook with Mom and wrote about painting Grandma's nails.

entries.title: Flashlight reading in bed
entries.body: Now I read in bed every night before I go to sleep. I have a little flashlight shaped like a cat and I read under the covers. Tonight I read four chapters of a book about a girl who finds a dragon egg. It has chapters, like Brett's books. Mommy came in and said lights out, but I said one more page, and she let me. Then I said one more page again, and she said Sunny.
entries.highlight: Has started reading chapter books in bed each night with a cat-shaped flashlight.

entries.title: Twenty books, twenty bears
entries.body: I filled up my whole reading chart for April! Twenty books. Mommy said the prize was a gummy bear for every book. So I lined up twenty gummy bears on the table in a long row, like a parade. I didn't eat them all at once. I ate five today and saved the rest in a jar. A year ago I just ate them really fast. Now I know how to make them last.
entries.highlight: Completed her April reading chart of twenty books and earned twenty gummy bears, choosing to save most of them.

entries.title: A robin's nest on the porch
entries.body: There is a robin's nest on top of our porch light! Daddy lifted me up very carefully and I peeked in and there are three blue eggs. They are the bluest blue, like a crayon. Daddy said we can't touch it or the mama will be upset. So now we use the back door. I made a sign for the front door that says quiet, baby birds. The mama robin watches us from the fence.
entries.highlight: Discovered a robin's nest with three blue eggs on the porch light and made a sign asking for quiet.

entries.title: Brett turned twelve
entries.body: Today is Brett's birthday and he is twelve! I picked his present by myself at the bookstore. It's a book about the funniest jokes in the world, because he always makes me laugh. I wrapped it myself with only a little bit too much tape. At dinner he read the jokes out loud. Why did the cow cross the road? To get to the udder side. Brett says twelve is almost a teenager. I hope he still plays with me.
entries.favorite: To get to the udder side
entries.highlight: Chose and wrapped a joke book for Brett's twelfth birthday and hoped he would still play with her as he grows up.

entries.title: The robin babies hatched
entries.body: The robin eggs hatched! When I came home from school I heard tiny peeping. Daddy lifted me up and there were three baby birds with no feathers and huge open mouths. They look a little bit like aliens. The mama keeps flying back with worms, real ones, not gummy ones. I've been checking every day since Sunday and I think I was a good neighbor because we kept quiet.
entries.highlight: Saw that the robin eggs on the porch had hatched into three baby birds after days of checking.

entries.title: A Mother's Day letter
entries.body: Sunday is Mother's Day, so tonight I wrote mommy a real letter. Last year I made a card and Brett helped me hide it. This year I wrote it all myself, a whole page. I wrote that mommy gives the best cuddles and does the best nails and she helps me when my feelings are tight. I wrote that I love her more than a thousand cats. That's a lot. I hid it in the secret notebook so she'll find it Sunday.
entries.highlight: Wrote Mom a full-page Mother's Day letter on her own, a step beyond last year's card made with Brett's help.

entries.title: Watching the thunderstorm
entries.body: There was a big thunderstorm tonight. When I was little I used to hide under my covers when it thundered. Tonight mommy and I sat by the window and counted between the lightning and the thunder. One, two, three, boom. Mommy said if you count higher, the storm is farther away. By the end we counted to eight, so it was leaving. I was only a little bit scared at the very loud one. I wasn't hiding.
entries.highlight: Watched a thunderstorm from the window with Mom and counted the seconds between lightning and thunder instead of hiding.

entries.title: Reading to the preschoolers
entries.body: Today my class went to the preschool room down the hall and we each read a book to a little kid. My little kid was named Rosie and she was four. She was shy and held her blanket. I read her a book about a bunny and I did the voices like Brett does. I told her I cried at preschool too, but then it got better. She smiled at me. It's funny, I used to be the little one.
entries.favorite: I used to be the little one
entries.highlight: Read a book to a shy four-year-old in the preschool room and comforted her by sharing her own preschool memories.

entries.title: Planting Sunny flowers
entries.body: On Sunday mommy and I planted sunflowers along the back fence. Mommy calls them Sunny flowers. The seeds are striped like little zebras. We poked them in the dirt a finger deep and watered them. Mommy said they might grow taller than daddy by the end of summer. I measured myself against the fence with a marker so I can see who's taller, me or the sunflowers. I bet the sunflowers will win but I'm growing too.
entries.highlight: Planted sunflowers with Mom along the back fence and marked her own height to compare over the summer.

entries.title: Homemade juice popsicles
entries.body: Brett showed me how to make our own popsicles. You pour juice into the popsicle molds and put the sticks in and freeze them overnight. I made grape ones, purple of course, and Brett made orange. I wanted to check every hour. Brett said a watched popsicle never freezes. After school today they were ready, and we ate them on the porch steps. Mine tasted like grape juice, which makes sense, because it is.
entries.highlight: Made homemade grape juice popsicles with Brett and ate them together on the porch.

entries.title: Grandma told me about grandpa
entries.body: It was Memorial Day and there was no school. We had a picnic at grandma's house. Grandma showed me a picture of grandpa when he was young, wearing a uniform. I never met him because he died before I was born. Grandma said he loved peanut butter cookies and silly jokes, like Brett. Her eyes got shiny, so I held her hand and didn't say anything for a minute. Then she said he would have loved me.
entries.highlight: Heard stories about her late grandfather on Memorial Day and quietly comforted Grandma by holding her hand.

entries.title: Almost the end of kindergarten
entries.body: It's the last week of kindergarten and I'm so tired from field day practice and cleaning out my cubby. When I got home I just laid on the couch with Puffball the toy on my tummy. Mommy asked if I'm sad kindergarten is ending. I said a little bit, because I'll miss Mrs. Lee and the turtle rug, but I'm also excited for summer and for first grade. You can feel two things. I learned that this year.
entries.highlight: Rested at home during the last week of kindergarten and talked with Mom about feeling both sad and excited.

entries.title: End of year cupcakes
entries.body: We had our end of the year party in class. Ben's mom brought cupcakes with blue frosting and Zoe's mom brought watermelon. We signed each other's shirts with markers. I wrote Sunny on everybody's shirt with a little sun next to it. Mrs. Lee hugged every single kid at the door. When she hugged me, she said, I knew you'd be brave. I didn't cry until I got in the car, and then only a little.
entries.highlight: Celebrated the end of kindergarten with cupcakes and signed shirts, and Mrs. Lee told her she knew she would be brave.

entries.title: Summer bucket list
entries.body: Kindergarten is over! Today is Sunday, my day, because it's kind of my name, and mommy and I made a summer bucket list on a big poster. Number one, ride my bike to the end of the street by myself. Number two, swim without my swim vest. Number three, ride a real pony. Number four, sleep over at grandma's. Number five, eat strawberry ice cream twenty times. I wrote it all myself and taped it on the fridge. Brett added number six, beat Brett at checkers. Ha ha.
entries.highlight: Wrote a summer bucket list with Mom, including riding her bike alone, swimming without her swim vest, and a night at Grandma's.

entries.title: First summer morning at grandma's
entries.body: This summer I go to grandma's house some mornings while mommy works. Today was the first day. Grandma and I had toast with her strawberry jam and then I watered her garden with the big hose. The seeds from the egg cartons are tall now and planted outside, and my popsicle stick labels are still there. The tomatoes have tiny yellow flowers. Grandma said, see, everything grows if you're patient. I'm getting a little better at patient.
entries.highlight: Spent her first summer morning at Grandma's, watering the garden where their egg carton seedlings are now growing.

entries.title: Practice for the end of the street
entries.body: After dinner mommy and I went out for bike practice because of number one on my bucket list. I rode to the third house without stopping, and I didn't even look down at my feet. Turning around is still the hardest part because the training wheels go bumpy on the grass. Mommy walks next to me but she doesn't hold anything anymore. She said, by next weekend you'll make it. I said, maybe even this weekend.
entries.highlight: Practiced bike riding after dinner with Mom walking beside her, working toward riding to the end of the street alone.

entries.title: Brett taught me to pump
entries.body: Today was Brett's last day of sixth grade, so he's going to be in seventh grade. After school he took me to the park, just me and him. He taught me how to pump my legs on the swing so I don't need anybody to push me. Legs out when you go forward, legs tucked when you go back. At first I just wiggled, but then I went higher and higher. Brett said soon I won't need him for anything. I said I'll always need you for reading the scary parts.
entries.favorite: I'll always need you for the scary parts
entries.highlight: Learned to pump her legs on the swing from Brett at the park on his last day of sixth grade.

entries.title: I rode my bike to the end of the street!
entries.body: I rode my bike all by myself to the end of the street! Number one on my bucket list, done. Last year on this exact day I rode my scooter to the end of the street, and now it's my bike. Mommy stayed at our driveway this time and didn't walk next to me at all. I pedaled past the yellow house and past the barking dog and I turned around at the stop sign without stopping. When I came back, mommy clapped so loud the neighbor came out to look. I crossed it off the list with a big purple marker.
entries.highlight: Rode her bike with training wheels to the end of the street and back entirely on her own, exactly a year after her first solo scooter ride.

entries.title: Riding bikes with Brett
entries.body: In the evening Brett got his bike out and we rode together around the block. He went in front and looked back at me every few houses. When we got home he gave me a high five and said remember when you used to race me on your scooter? I said I still beat you. He said not on a bike, Sunny Bunny. Next year I want to take the training wheels off so I can go as fast as him. Brett said he'll teach me, the same way daddy taught him.
entries.highlight: Rode bikes around the block with Brett for the first time and talked about taking her training wheels off next year.

entries.title: Signing up for summer reading
entries.body: My legs were tired from all the bike riding, so today was a cozy day. Mommy took me to the library to sign up for the summer reading club. You get a paper with fifty squares, and every time you read for twenty minutes you color in a square. I already did two squares on the beanbag in the kids room. Then we came home and I read on the porch swing until dinner. The librarian remembered me from story time when I was four.
entries.highlight: Joined the library's summer reading club and spent a restful day reading after a big weekend of bike riding.

entries.title: I beat Brett at checkers
entries.body: Tonight I beat Brett at checkers for real! It's number six on my bucket list, the one Brett wrote as a joke. I got three kings and I trapped his last piece in the corner so it couldn't move. Brett looked at the board for a long time and then he said, did you let me lose? I said no, I won. He asked if I wanted to play again right away, and I said no, I'm going to stay the champion tonight.
entries.highlight: Beat Brett at checkers for the first time, checking off the joke item he had added to her summer bucket list.

entries.title: Fireflies in a jar
entries.body: When it got dark, the fireflies came out over the backyard grass. They blink on and off like tiny flashlights. I caught one in my hands and it tickled. Then daddy gave me a jar with holes in the lid and I caught three more. I watched them blink in the jar for a few minutes and then I let them go, because they belong outside and their families would miss them. Daddy said that was kind. I named the brightest one Twinkle before it flew away.
entries.highlight: Caught fireflies in a jar with Dad and chose to release them so they could return to their families.

entries.title: The butterfly house
entries.body: We went to the butterfly house at the garden. It's warm and wet inside like a jungle, and there are hundreds of butterflies flying around. A blue one landed on mommy's hat and stayed there for the whole walk. I saw an orange and black one just like the ones from my class, and I told the lady we raised those in kindergarten. She said I must be an expert. I held my finger very still with juice on it, and one landed and drank it.
entries.highlight: Visited a butterfly house, recognized the species her class raised, and had a butterfly land on her finger.

entries.title: Lemonade stand with Ava
entries.body: In the afternoon Ava and I had a lemonade stand at the end of my driveway. We made a sign that said Lemonade 50 Cents, Cookies Too. I wrote the sign and Ava drew lemons. We stirred the lemonade with a big spoon and the neighbors came. I counted the money in quarters. We made seven dollars and fifty cents! We split it, and I used some of mine to buy strawberry ice cream with rainbow sprinkles for me and for Ava. She always gets chocolate, but she tried strawberry and loved it.
entries.favorite: Ava tried strawberry and loved it
entries.highlight: Ran a lemonade stand with Ava, counted their earnings in quarters, and treated Ava to strawberry ice cream.

entries.title: Father's Day French toast
entries.body: Today was Father's Day and it was also a Sunday, which is sort of my name, so it was double special. Mommy and I made daddy French toast and I flipped two pieces myself with the big spatula. One flew a little bit but it landed back in the pan. I brought daddy breakfast in bed and he said it was the best French toast he's ever had. Then we stayed in pajamas and played board games all morning. Daddy let me pick every game. I picked the cat one every time.
entries.favorite: The French toast landed back in the pan
entries.highlight: Made Father's Day French toast, flipping two herself, and spent a slow Sunday morning playing games with Dad.

entries.title: Snack bar after swim practice
entries.body: Mommy and I went to the outdoor pool and I practiced swimming without my swim vest in the shallow part. I can kick and paddle about five strokes before I have to stand up. Last summer I couldn't even put my face in. After practicing, mommy bought me a bag of gummy bears from the snack bar and we sat on the warm towels. My fingers were wrinkly like grandma's. I think I'll be able to swim without my vest by the end of summer.
entries.favorite: Five strokes without my swim vest
entries.highlight: Practiced swimming without her swim vest at the outdoor pool, managing about five strokes, then shared gummy bears with Mom.

entries.title: I rode a real pony
entries.body: At the county fair I rode a real pony! Number three on my bucket list. Her name was Daisy and she was brown with a white star on her nose. When I was little I pretended Sparkle the unicorn horse took me everywhere, and now I was on a real one. The man helped me up and I held the saddle horn. She walked in a big circle three times. I was nervous at first because she was so tall, but I patted her neck and said good girl. I think grandma's pony Buttons would have liked her.
entries.highlight: Rode a real pony at the county fair, a dream that began with her pretend unicorn horse Sparkle.

entries.title: Drawing Daisy for grandma
entries.body: Today I rested after the fair and drew a picture of me riding Daisy the pony. I drew her white star and my helmet and the circle we walked in. Then we went to grandma's and I gave it to her and told her everything. Grandma said she rode Buttons in a circle just like that when she was six. We're the same age at the same thing, sixty years apart or something. Grandma put the picture on her fridge right next to my rainbow from preschool.
entries.favorite: Next to my rainbow from preschool
entries.highlight: Drew her pony ride for Grandma, who shared that she rode her own pony at the same age.

entries.title: Making jam with grandma
entries.body: At grandma's this morning we made raspberry jam. Grandma used to do everything but now her wrists hurt, so I mashed the raspberries with the potato masher and she stirred the pot on the stove. I'm not allowed to do the hot part. I wrote the labels for the jars, Raspberry Jam by Grandma and Sunny, July. We made six jars. Grandma said one is for me to keep on my own shelf. My hands are pink from the berries.
entries.highlight: Made raspberry jam with Grandma, doing the mashing and labeling while Grandma handled the stove.

entries.title: Red, white and blue popsicles
entries.body: Mommy and I made striped popsicles for the Fourth of July. First we poured strawberry juice and froze it, then yogurt for the white, then blueberry for the blue. You have to wait for each layer to freeze, so it took all day. Brett said a watched popsicle never freezes again, and I said I know, I'm not watching, I'm just checking. They came out with wobbly stripes. I'm saving them for the fireworks.
entries.highlight: Made layered red, white and blue popsicles with Mom for the Fourth of July.

entries.title: Fireworks without covering my ears
entries.body: Last night we watched the fireworks from the park on a blanket. Last year I cried and grandma covered my ears. This year I sat by myself next to grandma and I only covered my ears for the really big booms at the end. I ate my striped popsicle and watched the colors. My favorite was the one that looked like a weeping willow tree. Today was a lazy Sunday because we stayed up so late, and I slept until nine.
entries.highlight: Watched Fourth of July fireworks while sitting on her own, covering her ears only at the finale, a year after crying at them.

entries.title: Camping in the backyard
entries.body: Brett and I set up the tent in the backyard and slept outside! Daddy helped with the poles. We brought sleeping bags, flashlights, and a bag of gummy bears. Brett told a story about a ghost cat, but I knew he was making it up because it had a dragon in it too. We heard crickets and an owl. I woke up in the middle of the night and Brett was snoring. I wasn't scared. I just listened to the owl until I fell back asleep.
entries.highlight: Camped overnight in the backyard tent with Brett and wasn't scared when she woke up in the dark.

entries.title: Chasing the ice cream truck
entries.body: The ice cream truck came down our street playing its song. I ran inside and got coins from my lemonade stand jar. I counted them quickly, four quarters and five dimes, a dollar fifty. I ran back out and waved and it stopped! They didn't have strawberry, so I got a rocket pop. The man said I counted my money faster than most grown ups. I ate it on the curb and it melted down to my elbow, just like when I was little.
entries.highlight: Bought a treat from the ice cream truck with her own lemonade stand money after quickly counting her coins.

entries.title: My first night at grandma's
entries.body: I slept over at grandma's house for the first time without mommy! Number four on my bucket list. I packed my own bag with pajamas, my toothbrush, my cat flashlight, and Puffball the toy. Grandma and I ate grilled cheese and played Old Maid, and I won, and this time I don't think she let me. At bedtime I missed mommy a little bit and my eyes got wet. Grandma sang me the bird on the fence song and I fell asleep. In the morning I was proud.
entries.favorite: This time I don't think she let me
entries.highlight: Spent her first night away from Mom at Grandma's house, managing a moment of missing Mom with Grandma's help.

entries.title: I swam without my swim vest
entries.body: I swam all the way across the shallow end without my swim vest! Number two on my bucket list. Mommy stood at the other side and I kicked and paddled and breathed to the side like the swim teacher showed me. It felt so far away, but I didn't stand up once. When I touched the wall, mommy picked me up and spun me around in the water. Last summer I was too scared to even put my face in. Now I can swim. That's a big change.
entries.favorite: Mommy spun me around in the water
entries.highlight: Swam across the shallow end of the pool without a swim vest for the first time, checking off a summer goal.

entries.title: Lake day with mommy
entries.body: Today was a mommy and me day at the lake. We packed a picnic with sandwiches cut in triangles and grapes and her famous lemon cookies. We floated on a big tube together and talked about everything, like first grade, and if ducks sleep, and why grandma is getting slower. Mommy said grandma is getting older, and that's why my helping matters so much. I found a smooth flat rock and tried to skip it. It sank, but mommy said next time.
entries.highlight: Spent a lake day with Mom, talking about first grade and Grandma getting older while floating on a tube.

entries.title: Pajama reading marathon
entries.body: It's Sunday, so I had a reading marathon in my pajamas. I read on my bed, then on the couch, then on the porch swing, then in Fort Sunny. I colored in six squares on my summer reading paper. I finished a chapter book about a girl who runs a pet hotel, which is basically my dream job. Mommy brought me snacks so I didn't have to stop. Sunday is still my favorite day, and not only because it's kind of my name.
entries.favorite: A pet hotel is my dream job
entries.highlight: Spent a Sunday reading in her pajamas in every cozy spot in the house and finished a chapter book.

entries.title: Fort Sunny got smaller
entries.body: It rained all day so Brett and I built Fort Sunny again in the living room. But it felt so small this time. My legs stuck out the end. Brett said the fort didn't get smaller, we got bigger. So we used the extra blankets and both couches and made it twice as big. We played cards inside with the flashlight. I changed the password from gummy bear to rainbow sprinkles, because I'm six now and that's more grown up.
entries.highlight: Rebuilt Fort Sunny with Brett on a rainy day, made it bigger because they had outgrown it, and updated the password.

entries.title: Making strawberry ice cream
entries.body: Daddy got an ice cream maker and we made our own strawberry ice cream! We used strawberries and cream and sugar. I mashed the strawberries and then we poured everything into the machine and it churned for a long time. It came out pink, real pink, not food coloring. We put rainbow sprinkles on top, like at the shop. Daddy said it's even better than the shop's. I said it's tied. Brett said it's the best and had seconds.
entries.highlight: Made homemade strawberry ice cream with Dad that came out naturally pink.

entries.title: Only the red tomatoes
entries.body: At grandma's this morning I picked tomatoes from the plants we grew from the egg carton seeds. I only picked the red ones this time. I remember last summer I picked a green one and grandma said it's not ready, like you're not ready to drive. I told her that joke and she laughed and said I have a memory like an elephant. Then I made us tomato sandwiches all by myself with a butter knife. Grandma said it was the best lunch all week.
entries.highlight: Harvested ripe tomatoes from the plants she and Grandma started from seed and made lunch for them both.

entries.title: A bracelet for Brett's camp
entries.body: Brett is going to sleepaway camp for a whole week starting on Saturday. I'm going to miss him so much. So I made him a friendship bracelet with purple and green string, because green is his favorite. It took me two days and the knots are a little crooked. I told him to wear it so he remembers me. He put it on right away and said he won't take it off, even in the lake. He said I can sleep in his room while he's gone if I want.
entries.favorite: He won't take it off, even in the lake
entries.highlight: Made Brett a friendship bracelet before he leaves for a week of sleepaway camp.

entries.title: Writing a letter for camp
entries.body: Mommy said we can send letters to Brett at camp, so I wrote one tonight so it gets there while he's there. Dear Brett, I hope you are having fun. Did you see any bears? I am going to sleep in your room. Don't worry, I won't touch your stuff. Maybe a little. Love, Sunny Bunny. I drew a picture of me holding a sign that said come home soon. Mommy said it's a very good letter, and she only fixed one word.
entries.favorite: I won't touch your stuff, maybe a little
entries.highlight: Wrote a letter to Brett at sleepaway camp on her own, with Mom correcting only one word.

entries.title: A real nail salon
entries.body: Mommy took me to a real nail salon for the first time! I sat in the big chair and the lady soaked my feet in bubbly water. She asked what color and I picked lavender with tiny white flowers on my big toes. Mommy got red. It tickled when she scrubbed my feet and I giggled so loud. It was fancy, but I told mommy that I still like it best when she does my nails at home on the couch.
entries.favorite: Tiny white flowers on my big toes
entries.highlight: Got her first professional pedicure with Mom but said she still prefers Mom painting her nails at home.

entries.title: Brett's camp stories
entries.body: Brett came home from camp yesterday and he was so tan and smelled like a campfire. Tonight we sat in Fort Sunny and he told me all his camp stories. He did a ropes course and canoed across the lake and his cabin had a raccoon get in. He still had my bracelet on, and it's a little faded from the lake. He said he read my letter three times. I liked having him back. His room was too quiet without him.
entries.highlight: Listened to Brett's camp stories in Fort Sunny and was happy to see him still wearing her bracelet.

entries.title: The sunflowers beat me
entries.body: Mommy and I measured the sunflowers against my marker line on the fence. The sunflowers are way taller than me now, taller than daddy even, just like mommy said. The biggest one has a flower bigger than my face. But I grew too! My new line is a whole inch higher than the line from May. Mommy wrote the date next to it. I said I lost to the sunflowers but at least I beat my old self.
entries.highlight: Measured herself against the sunflowers she and Mom planted in May and found she had grown an inch.

entries.title: Dinosaurs at the museum
entries.body: Saturday was a mommy and me day at the science museum. There was a giant dinosaur skeleton and I read the sign by myself. It said it was as long as a school bus. I told mommy grandma's joke about the dinosaurs on her first day of school. We went in a room where you make bubbles as big as you, and I stood inside one. We ate lunch at the cafe and I ordered for both of us.
entries.highlight: Visited the science museum with Mom, read the exhibit signs herself, and ordered lunch for both of them.

entries.title: All fifty reading squares
entries.body: I colored the last square on my summer reading paper! Fifty squares, so that's a thousand minutes of reading. That's as many as a thousand cats, but minutes. Mommy took me to the library to turn it in, and I got to pick a free book from the prize shelf. I picked a book about a cat who becomes a detective, like Inspector Whiskers that Brett read me. Then I came home and started it in the hammock. I'm already on chapter three.
entries.highlight: Completed all fifty squares of the library summer reading club and chose a prize chapter book.

entries.title: Peach cobbler for grandma
entries.body: Mom and I bought peaches at the farmers market and made peach cobbler. I peeled the peaches with a peeler. Mom showed me how to go away from my fingers. Then I sprinkled the crumble on top. It smelled so good in the oven. We took half of it to grandma. Grandma said peach cobbler was her mother's favorite. That's my great grandma, I think. I like that our recipes go back so far.
entries.favorite: Our recipes go back so far
entries.highlight: Peeled peaches and helped bake a cobbler with Mom, then shared it with Grandma.

entries.title: Picking my first day outfit
entries.body: Mom took me shopping for first grade clothes and I picked my first day outfit all by myself. A purple shirt with a sun on it and a jean skirt and new sneakers with laces, not velcro, because I can tie them. Mom asked if I want a new backpack, but I said no, I'm keeping my cat one because it's lucky. I'm going to wear grandma's ribbon again too. Mom said I know exactly who I am.
entries.highlight: Chose her own first grade outfit, picked lace-up sneakers, and decided to keep her lucky cat backpack.

entries.title: Thinking about first grade
entries.body: I laid in the hammock with Brett this afternoon and we talked about first grade. My teacher is going to be Mr. Grant. I've never had a boy teacher. Brett had him too and said he does magic tricks on Fridays and has a pet snake in the classroom. A snake! I'm a little nervous about the snake. But I'm not nervous about saying goodbye to mom anymore. That used to be the hardest part. Now the hardest part is the snake.
entries.highlight: Talked with Brett about her upcoming first grade teacher and noted that saying goodbye to Mom no longer worries her.

entries.title: Last summer morning at grandma's
entries.body: Today was my last summer morning at grandma's house before school. I made grandma lunch by myself, a turkey sandwich cut in triangles, and I poured her iced tea. I brought it to her on a tray because her back was sore. She said, who is this grown up lady in my kitchen? Then she gave me a little notebook with a cat on it and said, for writing your first grade stories. I'm going to write my first one about her.
entries.favorite: Who is this grown up lady in my kitchen
entries.highlight: Made and served Grandma lunch on her last summer morning there, and Grandma gave her a notebook for first grade stories.

entries.title: First day of first grade
entries.body: First day of first grade! I wore my sun shirt, my lace-up sneakers, and grandma's purple ribbon, and I carried my lucky cat backpack. At the door I hugged mom and said you don't have to come in, and I walked in by myself. No butterflies, well, maybe one. Mr. Grant is tall and funny and he wears a bow tie. There was a new girl named Nora who looked scared, so I showed her where the cubbies are and sat with her. Then we painted pictures of ourselves. I painted myself with a big smile, like my sun from the first day of kindergarten.
entries.highlight: Started first grade with Mr. Grant, walked in on her own, and helped a nervous new classmate find her way.

entries.title: Telling grandma about Mr. Grant
entries.body: Grandma picked me up on Friday and we walked home slowly together. I told her all about my first week. Mr. Grant did a magic trick today where he turned a red scarf blue. Brett was right about the magic Fridays. And the snake is real. Her name is Slinky and she's a corn snake and she's orange and white. I haven't touched her yet. Grandma said she never touched a snake in eighty years and she's fine. I said I might beat you, grandma.
entries.highlight: Told Grandma about her first week of first grade, including Mr. Grant's magic trick and the class corn snake.

entries.title: My first story in grandma's notebook
entries.body: It's a long weekend because of Labor Day, so this morning I stayed in my pajamas and wrote my first story in the cat notebook grandma gave me. It's called The Grandma Who Had a Pony. It's about grandma when she was six and rode Buttons around the farm, and one day Buttons ran away to find apples, and grandma found him in the orchard. It's two whole pages. Some of it is true and some I made up. I'm going to read it to her next time.
entries.favorite: Some of it is true and some I made up
entries.highlight: Wrote a two-page story about Grandma and her childhood pony in the notebook Grandma gave her.

entries.title: Biking all the way to the park
entries.body: In the afternoon mom and I rode bikes all the way to the park, which is way past the end of our street. Mom rode her bike behind me. I stopped at every corner and looked both ways before crossing, even though mom was right there. At the park I had a snack on the bench and watched the ducks. The training wheels made a clicky noise on the path. Mom said next summer they come off. I said maybe even sooner.
entries.highlight: Rode her bike all the way to the park with Mom, stopping to check for traffic at every corner.

entries.title: Homework next to Brett
entries.body: It's Sunday and Brett had lots of seventh grade homework, so I sat next to him at the kitchen table and did my own homework too. Mine was a page of adding to ten and his was something about the Romans. I finished way faster. Then I just colored next to him so he wouldn't be lonely. He said, you know you don't have to stay. I said I know, I want to. He shared his pretzels with me.
entries.highlight: Kept Brett company while he did his seventh grade homework, finishing her own first and staying to color beside him.

entries.title: Ants on a log, made by me
entries.body: After school I made my own snack, ants on a log. You take celery and fill the middle with peanut butter, and then you put raisins on top for the ants. I used the butter knife and only made a little mess. I made one for Brett too, but he doesn't like raisins, so I made his with chocolate chips. Mom said that's not ants, that's something else. I said they're chocolate ants. They're the fancy kind.
entries.highlight: Made her own after-school snack of ants on a log, plus a custom chocolate chip version for Brett.

entries.title: Reader of the day
entries.body: Today I was the reader of the day in Mr. Grant's class. That means you sit in the special chair and read a book out loud to everybody during morning meeting. I picked my cat detective book. Twenty kids were looking at me, but I wasn't nervous, I was excited. I did the voices like Brett. When I finished, Mr. Grant said I read with a lot of expression. Nora asked if she can borrow the book. Last year at the sing-along my voice was shaky. This time it wasn't at all.
entries.favorite: Twenty kids looking and I wasn't nervous
entries.highlight: Read a chapter book aloud to her whole first grade class as reader of the day, confident and full of expression.

entries.title: A sign for Brett's soccer game
entries.body: Saturday was Brett's first soccer game of the season. I made a big sign with markers that said Go Brett, Number 7, you can do it. I wrote it all by myself and spelled everything right. I held it up and yelled every time he had the ball. He scored a goal in the second half and pointed at me in the stands! His friends asked who the loud kid was, and he said that's my sister. He sounded proud.
entries.favorite: He pointed at me in the stands
entries.highlight: Made a sign and cheered for Brett at his soccer game, and he pointed to her after scoring a goal.

entries.title: You can just drop me off
entries.body: This morning I told mom she doesn't have to walk me into school anymore. She can just drop me off at the car line like Brett. Mom got a little quiet and then said okay, but she gave me an extra squeeze hug first. I got out of the car and walked in with Nora and I waved at the door. After school mom told me she was proud but also a little sad that I'm growing up so fast. I told her I'll still need cuddles. Forever probably.
entries.favorite: I'll still need cuddles, forever probably
entries.highlight: Asked to be dropped off at the car line instead of walked in, and reassured Mom she would still want cuddles.

entries.title: Picking movie night
entries.body: Friday was family movie night and it was my turn to pick. It's the first chilly night so we had blankets and the big bowl of popcorn. I picked a movie about a girl and her horse, of course. Daddy fell asleep halfway through and was snoring, and Brett put a popcorn on his nose. I laughed so hard. At the end the girl rides the horse in a big race and wins. I'm going to ask for riding lessons for my birthday.
entries.favorite: Brett put a popcorn on daddy's nose
entries.highlight: Chose the family movie night film on the first chilly evening of fall and decided to ask for riding lessons.

entries.title: I held Slinky the snake
entries.body: I held Slinky the snake! Mr. Grant showed us how to hold her with two hands, one in the front and one in the middle, and let her slide through your fingers. She felt cool and smooth, not slimy at all. Her tongue flicked in and out, but Mr. Grant said she's just smelling. My heart was pounding at first, like with the goat. Now I've fed a goat and held a snake. I can't wait to tell grandma I beat her.
entries.favorite: She felt cool and smooth, not slimy
entries.highlight: Held the class corn snake for the first time, connecting it to how she overcame her fear of goats.

entries.title: Clover the neighbor's bunny
entries.body: Our neighbors Mr. and Mrs. Hughes got a bunny! Her name is Clover and she is white and fluffy, exactly like Puffball in my dreams. Mrs. Hughes said I can help feed her after school sometimes. Today I held her little leash and Clover hopped in front of me in the grass, bouncing like a cotton ball. She's not mine, but Mrs. Hughes said I can be her best friend. Clover doesn't have a bunny mansion, but she has a bed shaped like a little castle. That counts.
entries.highlight: Got to help care for the neighbors' new bunny, the closest thing yet to her long-held bunny wish.

entries.title: A rainy chapter book Friday
entries.body: It rained all Friday afternoon, and I was so happy to just be inside. I'm reading a series about two sisters who solve mysteries in their town. I'm on book three already. I read on the window seat with my fuzzy blanket and listened to the rain. When I was little I used to race the raindrops on the glass. I still did it a little today, between chapters. My raindrop lost, but my book is really good, so I didn't mind.
entries.highlight: Spent a rainy Friday on the window seat reading the third book in a mystery series.

entries.title: Winding grandma's yarn
entries.body: In the evening grandma came over and asked me to help her wind a ball of yarn. She held the yarn loop on her hands and I wound it around and around into a ball. Her hands get tired holding it up, so we switched and I held it and she wound. She's knitting a scarf for me, purple of course. She said it's a secret, but I saw the color. When I was little I made Sparkle a finger knitting scarf. Now grandma's making me a real one.
entries.favorite: She said it's a secret but I saw
entries.highlight: Helped Grandma wind yarn for a purple scarf Grandma is knitting for her.

entries.title: I read the recipe
entries.body: Mom and I made apple crisp after school, and this time I read the recipe out loud instead of mom. One fourth cup of brown sugar, one teaspoon of cinnamon, and half a cup of oats. I learned fractions are like cutting a pizza. I measured everything and leveled it with my finger like I learned in kindergarten. Mom just did the oven and cut the apples. She said soon I'll be making dinner for her. I said maybe just dessert.
entries.highlight: Read the apple crisp recipe aloud and measured all the ingredients while baking with Mom.

entries.title: Writing grandma's letter for her
entries.body: Grandma got a letter from her old friend Dottie, but her eyes were too tired to read the small handwriting. So I read it to her. Dottie has a new kitten and a bad knee. Then grandma said, will you write my letter back? She told me what to say and I wrote it all down in my neatest handwriting, a whole page. I only asked how to spell two words, which were wonderful and neighbors. Grandma signed her name at the bottom with her shaky hand. I feel like I'm her helper for real now, not pretend.
entries.favorite: Her helper for real now, not pretend
entries.highlight: Read a letter aloud to Grandma and then wrote Grandma's full-page reply as Grandma dictated it.

entries.title: A Sparkle costume
entries.body: Mom and I decided my Halloween costume. I'm going to be Sparkle, the unicorn horse I pretended about when I was little. Mom is making the costume with a white hoodie, and I drew the plan myself on paper. It has a rainbow mane made of yarn and a gold horn on the hood. Mom said, are you sure you're not too big for Sparkle? I said you're never too big for Sparkle. She's kind of part of me.
entries.favorite: You're never too big for Sparkle
entries.highlight: Designed her own Halloween costume as Sparkle, the pretend unicorn horse from her early childhood.

entries.title: Brett is still coming
entries.body: At dinner Brett said some of his friends think twelve is too old for trick or treating. I got worried that he won't come with me this year. But then he said, I'm still going, because somebody has to make sure Sunny doesn't eat all her candy on the sidewalk. He's going to be a cowboy so he can lead the unicorn. I'm really glad. Even when he's a teenager I want him to come with me.
entries.favorite: A cowboy to lead the unicorn
entries.highlight: Felt relieved when Brett, now twelve, said he would still go trick-or-treating with her dressed as a cowboy.

entries.title: Cider donuts at the orchard
entries.body: We had no school today, so we went to the apple orchard. I picked apples from the high branches by standing on daddy's shoulders. Then we got apple cider donuts that were still warm and covered in cinnamon sugar. The sugar got all over my sweater, like when I rolled snickerdoodles with grandma. The white horse was still by the fence, the one I named Sparkle Two last year. I'm pretty sure he remembered me. I gave him a piece of apple on my flat hand.
entries.highlight: Picked apples and ate warm cider donuts at the orchard, and fed the same white horse she met last year.

entries.title: First fire in the fireplace
entries.body: Tonight daddy made the first fire of the year in the fireplace. It crackles and pops, and the whole room smells like smoke and marshmallows, because we roasted some on long sticks. Mine caught on fire and I blew it out and ate it burnt. Burnt is actually good. Then I read my mystery book to mom, while she lay on the couch with her eyes closed. She said she was listening. I think she was a little bit asleep.
entries.highlight: Roasted marshmallows by the first fire of the season and read her mystery book aloud to Mom.

entries.title: Hayride and a caramel apple
entries.body: On Saturday we went to the pumpkin patch and rode the hayride. The hay is scratchy and gets in your socks. I picked a giant pumpkin that I couldn't lift, so Brett carried it and pretended he was going to drop it. Then I got a caramel apple with crushed nuts, and it was so sticky that I needed both hands and my face. The goats were there, and I fed them without even thinking about it. When I was four I hid behind daddy from them, and last fall I only waved from the fence.
entries.favorite: I fed the goats without thinking
entries.highlight: Enjoyed a hayride and a caramel apple at the pumpkin patch and fed the goats she once feared without hesitation.

entries.title: Carving pumpkins with Brett
entries.body: Brett and I carved our pumpkins tonight. Last year mom cut the top and I scooped the guts. This year Brett let me use the little carving saw, the kid safe one, and I carved my own pumpkin while he watched. I made a cat face with pointy ears and whiskers. One whisker broke off, so I made it a cat with three whiskers. Brett carved a unicorn on his to match my costume. It looks like a horse with a carrot on its head, but I love it.
entries.favorite: Brett carved a unicorn to match me
entries.highlight: Carved her own jack-o-lantern with a kid-safe saw while Brett carved a unicorn to match her costume.

entries.title: Gluing on the rainbow mane
entries.body: After pumpkins, mom and I worked on my Sparkle costume. Mom sewed the yarn mane onto the hood, and I glued on sequins all down the back, one at a time. It took forever and my fingers got sticky with glue. We put on music and talked while we worked. Mom said she remembered when I first told her about Sparkle, when I was four and said she was invisible but real. She said Sparkle grew up with me.
entries.highlight: Helped Mom finish her Sparkle costume by gluing on sequins while they reminisced about her pretend unicorn.

entries.title: I threaded the needle myself
entries.body: The gold horn on my costume came loose, so I took it to grandma, like last year when my kitty tail fell off. But this time I threaded the needle myself, because grandma's eyes are tired and my eyes are young. I licked the thread to make it pointy like she taught me. Then grandma sewed the horn back on tight. She said, last year you held the thread, and this year you did the hard part. I said, next year I'll do the sewing.
entries.favorite: This year you did the hard part
entries.highlight: Threaded the needle herself so Grandma could reattach her costume horn, a step up from just holding the thread last year.

entries.title: Grandma at the costume parade
entries.body: Today was the Halloween costume parade at school, and grandma came to watch! We walked around the whole playground in a line while the parents took pictures. I saw grandma sitting on a bench with her cane, and I galloped over to her like a real unicorn. She said that horn looks familiar. Mr. Grant was dressed as a wizard with a long beard. Nora was a butterfly. Grandma was clapping and cheering, and she stayed until the very end even though it was chilly.
entries.highlight: Galloped over to Grandma during the school Halloween costume parade, where Grandma stayed to cheer until the end.

entries.title: Halloween as Sparkle
entries.body: For Halloween I was Sparkle the unicorn horse, with the rainbow mane and the gold horn, and Brett was a cowboy leading me with a pretend rope. Last year I was a kitty and Brett held my bucket when it got too heavy. This year I carried my own bucket the whole night, even when it was super full, and I held Brett's flashlight for him. People kept saying, what a beautiful unicorn. I said thank you, I've been her for a long time. At the spooky house I walked up first.
entries.highlight: Went trick-or-treating as her childhood unicorn Sparkle with cowboy Brett, carrying her own bucket and leading the way at the spooky house.

entries.title: Reading to mommy under the stars
entries.body: The clocks changed again so it's dark at dinnertime. After dinner, mommy and I went outside with a blanket to look at the stars, like last year. This time I brought my flashlight and a book about space, and I read her facts while she pointed. The Big Dipper is part of a bigger shape called the Great Bear. I found it before she did. A blinking light went by and I said, that's an airplane, mommy, not a winking star. She laughed and said, you remembered.
entries.highlight: Stargazed with Mom after the time change, read space facts aloud, and found the Big Dipper first.

entries.title: The biggest leaf pile with Brett
entries.body: Brett and I raked leaves in the backyard after school. Brett has a phone now and he checks it a lot, and sometimes he doesn't want to play. But today he put it in his pocket and we made the biggest leaf pile ever. He threw me in it! We talked about Christmas, and he promised to take me snowboarding again when it snows. He said this year he'll teach me to go down the little hill on the snowboard, standing up, not sitting like when I was four.
entries.favorite: He put his phone in his pocket
entries.highlight: Raked and jumped in a giant leaf pile with Brett, who promised to teach her to snowboard standing up this winter.

entries.title: Grandma's birthday snickerdoodles
entries.body: Yesterday was grandma's birthday, so I made her snickerdoodles from the recipe card I copied in my own handwriting. Mom helped with the oven, but I measured everything and rolled every ball in the cinnamon sugar. When I gave them to grandma, she took one bite and said they taste exactly like mine. Then she said, the recipe really does live in two kitchens now. After, daddy took me for strawberry ice cream with rainbow sprinkles, even though it's November. Some things I like are the same as when I was little. Some things are new. I like both.
entries.highlight: Baked snickerdoodles for Grandma's birthday from her own handwritten copy of Grandma's recipe, and Grandma said they tasted just like hers.

entries.title: Helping grandma
entries.body: After school I helped grandma in her garden because she is old and her back hurts when she bends down. I pulled weeds from around her flowers and the tomato plants we grew, the big ones with long roots that come out with a pop. I put them all in a bucket. When we were done she gave me a cookie, a snickerdoodle, and we sat on the porch swing. She told me a story about when mommy was little and climbed the apple tree and got stuck, and grandpa had to get the ladder.
entries.highlight: Pulled weeds in Grandma's garden to spare Grandma's back and heard a story about Mom getting stuck in a tree as a child.

entries.title: A resting day
entries.body: My perfect day was resting. I stayed in my pajamas all day long, even at lunch, and I cuddled with mommy on the couch under the fuzzy blanket. We didn't go anywhere or do anything busy. In the afternoon Brett read me a book, the second dragon book about Ember, even though I can read it myself now. I just like his voices. It was Sunday, my favorite day, partly because it's kind of my name, and partly because it's the day everybody slows down.
entries.highlight: Spent a restful Sunday in pajamas cuddling with Mom while Brett read aloud from a favorite dragon book.
